32 cloud tests are env-gated (ADPORT_RUN_DATABASE_TESTS, ADPORT_SELECTION_TEST_DATABASE_URL, ADPORT_HTTP_TEST_BASE_URL) and 3 engine tests (PAID_MEDIA_LIVE_TESTS); none runs anywhere automatically, and the leftover .env.local makes the DB suites fail with ECONNREFUSED instead of skipping.
http.integration.test.ts has 2 of 6 cases that cannot pass against a current server (scopes: [] vs the mcp-oauth-repository scope filter); known, documented, unfixed.
No automated test runs cloud code against the engine host; the cloud<->engine contract is held by hand-written fixtures and unvalidated JSON casts (currently aligned by inspection).

The approval-gate authorization routes (apply/reject), runAssistantTurn and the demo/live runtime switch have zero automated coverage despite being the enforcement point of the 'human approves' invariant.

Stripe webhook/signature/entitlement chain, real OAuth exchanges, the compose-default engine Postgres persistence path, and the Playwright E2E cited in phase reports all lack automated or reproducible tests.

The script is byte-identical to upstream and Playwright is not a dependency of either tree, so it cannot be executed from the repository.

findings.title: No CI pipeline runs any markting-ai test; vendored upstream workflows are inert
findings.description: GitHub Actions only reads /.github/workflows; the upstream workflows under platform/ and engine/ never fire. make test (53 vitest + 7 pytest + 3 node cases) and the 308-case cloud suite run only when invoked manually.
findings.recommendation: Add a root workflow: make test; pnpm test/typecheck/build in platform/; uv pytest in engine/; an e2e job behind supabase start.

findings.title: Documented happy path relied on self-approval; .env.example ships demo mode and self-approval enabled by default
findings.description: The apply route refuses when requester == approver unless MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true. The seed creates one user, so the reported 'Apply → row gone' is only reachable with that flag on (INFERRED for the specific run). The requester≠approver control therefore has no end-to-end evidence and no route-level test. Separately, .env.example defaults MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=true and MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true, so a deployment copied from it runs the sandbox provider behind the real Approvals page and lets requesters approve their own changes.
findings.recommendation: E2E matrix must run with two users and self-approval off (assert 403 for requester, success for second user). Ship .env.example with both flags false and let the demo seed/make target flip them; warn at boot when either is true outside development.

findings.title: Engine report runs are not tenant-scoped: any signed-in user of any organization lists and downloads every run
findings.description: The cloud route only checks the caller has some membership, then proxies the engine's single global report index and any rpt_*/art_* file. A two-tenant e2e scenario would fail today. Impact is limited to run metadata because the engine host refuses to start unless PAID_MEDIA_DATA_MODE=sample, so file contents are synthetic; this becomes P0 if that assertion is ever relaxed.
findings.recommendation: Scope the engine report surface by organization (per-org index or org-prefixed names) and add the two-tenant scenario to the e2e matrix.

findings.title: UI has no stable test hooks and Apply uses window.confirm
findings.description: Every visible string is translated and Arabic by default, so text/aria selectors need per-locale tables; the native confirm dialog requires dialog handling in every apply spec. Any future suite will be brittle without locale-independent hooks.
findings.recommendation: Add data-testid on the ~15 interaction points listed in the report's scenario table and replace window.confirm with an in-page confirm element.

The documented 'Apply → row gone' path depends on MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true; .env.example ships that and MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=true as defaults, so the requester≠approver control is unverified and demo code is reachable in production configuration (P2).

findings.title: Engine report list/download has no tenant scoping; any signed-in user of any org reads every report
evidence: harness: reports GET org B viewer => 200; report file org B viewer => 200 (engine URL http://engine.test/reports, no org)
findings.description: Routes pass organizationId only to resolve membership; the engine keeps one global report index with requested_by always the service caller. A viewer in org B lists and downloads org A's runs. Data is fixture-only today because serve_demo forces PAID_MEDIA_DATA_MODE=sample (serve_demo.py:163-166,183-191,383-388), so impact is P2 now and P0 the moment real data is wired.
findings.recommendation: Namespace runs and files per organization (or one engine token per org), filter GET /reports by requester, bind downloads to the run's organization before non-fixture data is ever used.

findings.title: Viewer/reader-plan user asking the Assistant for a change gets 403 after the engine paused; proposal orphaned, text lost
evidence: harness: assistant viewer receives proposal => 403; recordEngineProposal calls: 0; engine reject calls: 0
findings.description: The tools:write check runs only after the engine produced an awaiting_approval proposal. The turn fails, no provenance is recorded, the engine is never told the proposal was handled, and the assistant's text is discarded. Affects every viewer and every org on the default free reader plan.
findings.recommendation: Check scopes before contacting the engine for write intent, or convert the proposal into an unsupported/not_allowed bridge outcome while still performing the hand-off and returning the assistant text.

findings.title: Requesting a non-member organizationId returns 500 Internal server error (and logs) instead of 403
evidence: harness: apply wrong org => 500; reject wrong org => 500; reports GET wrong org => 500 (1 console.error each)
findings.description: resolveMembership throws a plain Error; routes only translate 'Authentication required.' so the membership failure maps to 500 with server-error logging. Membership is still enforced; no data leaks.
findings.recommendation: Throw HttpError 403 from resolveMembership or translate it in a shared helper used by all session routes.

findings.title: Engine error translation inconsistent: 4xx engine details leak verbatim, engine 401 relayed as user 401, friendly 5xx messages are dead code
evidence: harness: reports GET engine 401 => 401 {"error":"Engine returned 401: {\"detail\":\"invalid bearer token\"}"}; reports POST engine 422 => 422 with pydantic detail; reports GET engine unreachable => 503 {"error":"Internal server error."}
findings.description: A misconfigured MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN surfaces to end users as HTTP 401 with engine detail text; validation/conflict bodies are forwarded raw; the curated 'engine not reachable' messages can never reach a client because apiError rewrites every >=500 body.
findings.recommendation: Map engine errors to a fixed vocabulary (502/503 + stable code), never relay engine 401/403 as user auth statuses, let apiError keep curated 5xx messages.

findings.title: Apply is not atomic: concurrent applies of one pending id can execute the provider write twice
findings.description: PolicyEngine.apply does get -> applyWrite -> delete with no claim; PostgresPendingStore.delete is an unconditional update with no consumed_at-is-null guard or affected-row check. Two approvers or a retry while the first call is in flight can both pass get and both call provider.applyWrite (duplicate campaign creation, double budget write). Inherited from upstream adport; race outcome INFERRED, not reproduced. UI button disable mitigates accidental double click only.
findings.recommendation: Atomically consume the row before the provider call (update ... where consumed_at is null returning id; 409 on zero rows) and make PendingOperationStore.delete report whether it consumed.

findings.title: Report runs are not plan-gated and effectively unlimited; one member can monopolise the shared engine lock
evidence: harness: reports POST member reader-plan => 200; reports POST cadence=yearly end=2026-13-99 => 200 with engine body {"cadence":"weekly","end":"2026-13-99"}
findings.description: Only viewers are refused; no requireScope or plan check; 120 runs/min per org; each run serialises under a process-wide asyncio.Lock and renders HTML/PDF; the 50-entry index is shared across orgs. Invalid end dates pass the regex and are forwarded (engine 422 leaked).
findings.recommendation: Gate POST /api/reports/engine on a plan entitlement, lower the per-org limit, validate end as a real date, return 409/429 when the engine lock is busy.

findings.title: Provider write succeeds but client is told it failed when post-write bookkeeping throws
evidence: harness: apply write ok, provenance update fails => 500; applyPending called: 1
findings.description: markPendingOutcome runs after applyPending without isolation; on failure the approver sees 'could not apply', the pending row is already consumed, a retry returns 404 and the row disappears from Approvals. Only the applied audit event reflects the truth.
findings.recommendation: Treat provenance update as best-effort (log, still return ok with result) or persist it with the pending consume in one transaction.

findings.title: Body handling on session POST routes: malformed JSON silently accepted, null body 500, no content-type/origin check, no size cap
evidence: harness: apply bad JSON => 200; apply body=null => 500; apply text/plain body (origin evil.example) => 200; apply 5MB body => 200; reports POST bad JSON => 200 (run triggered); v1 tools bad JSON => 500
findings.description: Five hand-rolled request.json().catch(() => ({})) sites accept garbage and fall back to the default organization; null body crashes to 500; only /api/waitlist checks Origin and bounds the stream; CSRF defence rests solely on SameSite=Lax. Next.js route-handler body ceiling is INFERRED unbounded (serverActions limit only).
findings.recommendation: One readJsonBody(request, schema, maxBytes) helper (zod, 400/413/415) for all session routes; reject cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site on mutating routes.

findings.title: /api/support maps every non-Zod failure to 403 and echoes raw error messages including DB connection details
evidence: harness: support DB error => 403 {"error":"connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.5:5432 relation \"public.feedback\" does not exist"}; support bad JSON => 403 with parser text; support unauthenticated => 403; support honeypot filled => 400 Zod issue naming website
findings.description: A fixed <500 status makes apiError return error.message verbatim, so infrastructure details reach signed-in users when the database misbehaves; missing session is 403 not 401; the honeypot is disclosed by the validation error (waitlist hides it).
findings.recommendation: Use the generic apiError(error) mapping so unknown errors are 500 with a fixed message, 401 for missing session, make the honeypot response indistinguishable from success.

findings.title: Requester-not-equal-approver rule exists only on the dashboard route and the shipped .env.example turns it off
findings.description: The four-eyes control described in docs/PHASE1-REPORT.md:16 applies only to the dashboard; REST/MCP second calls have no requester check; API-key-created rows have no creator and can be applied by any admin; every deployment created by following the README has self-approval enabled.
findings.recommendation: Default the flag to false in .env.example, enforce the rule in the REST/MCP second call (record created_by for API keys), document the remaining gap.

findings.title: /api/dashboard/summary collapses all failures into 400 and uses organization_id while every other route uses organizationId
evidence: harness: summary DB/provider throw => 400 {"error":"Unable to read provider data."}; summary ?organizationId=orgB => 200 with sessionPrincipal(undefined)

findings.title: Concurrent apply() with the same pending id executes the provider write twice
evidence: node double-apply.mjs => exit 0: statuses [fulfilled, fulfilled], applyWriteCalls 2, audit [validated, applied, applied]
findings.description: PolicyEngine.apply does pending.get -> hash/expiry checks -> provider.applyWrite -> audit -> pending.delete. Nothing claims the id before the provider mutation. PostgresPendingStore.delete is an unconditional update with no consumed_at-is-null predicate, no returning and no row-count check; the file store is equally unconditional. Two overlapping requests with one pending_operation_id (client retry, double click, MCP resend, two replicas) both pass get() and both call applyWrite. Reproduced at runtime with the file store; the Postgres SQL has the same shape (VERIFIED_CODE). The same repo already uses the correct for-update/consume pattern for OAuth state and MCP refresh tokens, and the Python engine claims before executing. Secondary: if audit.append or pending.delete throws after a successful applyWrite, the id stays live and can be replayed within TTL.
findings.recommendation: Add an atomic claim before provider.applyWrite: Postgres `update pending_operations set consumed_at=now() where id=$1 and organization_id=$2 and consumed_at is null and expires_at>now() returning ...` (zero rows -> PENDING_NOT_FOUND/EXPIRED); file store via rename/O_EXCL marker. Extend PendingOperationStore with claim() or make delete return a boolean. Add a concurrent Promise.all test with a slow mock applyWrite asserting exactly one provider call, plus a Postgres-backed equivalent. Kept at P1 (not P0) because default policy coerces created campaigns to PAUSED (engine.ts:55).

findings.title: Dashboard reject cannot stop an in-flight apply; rejected operation still executes
findings.description: Both routes read the pending row via listPendingOperations().find and then act. If Apply passes engine.apply's get() and Reject then sets consumed_at, Apply still proceeds to provider.applyWrite because nothing re-checks consumption. Audit shows rejected then applied for one id; markPendingOutcome is an unconditional update so status is last-writer-wins. Two concurrent Apply clicks are a direct instance of F6-01. Timing window is INFERRED; ordering is VERIFIED_CODE.
findings.recommendation: Same atomic claim as F6-01 so a reject that wins makes the apply fail with PENDING_NOT_FOUND; make markPendingOutcome conditional on current status.

findings.title: Budget policy not re-evaluated at apply time (validate->apply TOCTOU)
findings.description: apply() re-runs only checkStaticPolicy; checkBudgetPolicy runs only in validate() against fromMicros captured at preview time, and apply compares only the op hash. Within pending_ttl_minutes the live baseline can change (concurrent operator or pending op), so the percentage-delta rail can be exceeded relative to live state. The sandbox CAS compares state loaded inside applyWrite, not preview-time state, so it does not close this window either; real providers have no CAS.
findings.recommendation: In apply(), re-run previewWrite (or a cheap read) and re-apply checkBudgetPolicy, or fail with PENDING_MISMATCH when live baseline differs from preview.budgetDeltas[].fromMicros.

findings.title: Stripe webhook dedupe is check-then-act and ignores event ordering
findings.description: processStripeEvent selects billing_events by event_id, runs applySubscription, then inserts the marker with on conflict do nothing. Two concurrent deliveries of one event both process (duplicate subscription_updated audit rows). No event.created comparison, so an older subscription.updated arriving after a newer one overwrites plan/status (last-writer-wins). Only a single delivery is tested.
findings.recommendation: Insert the marker first with `on conflict do nothing returning event_id` (zero rows -> duplicate) inside the same transaction as applySubscription; skip events older than the last applied event timestamp.

findings.title: Postgres-backed concurrency tests exist but are never run by CI
evidence: grep for ADPORT_RUN_DATABASE_TESTS / ADPORT_SELECTION_TEST_DATABASE_URL across repo => no matches

Their correctness is therefore only VERIFIED_CODE by reading SQL.
findings.recommendation: Add a Postgres service container to both CI workflows and set the gating variables, or document the manual pre-release run and its evidence.

findings.title: Provider OAuth refresh lacks single-flight except LinkedIn; Microsoft rotates tokens without coalescing
findings.description: Google, Microsoft, Apple and Snapchat clients check accessToken.expiresAt then await a network refresh with no in-flight coalescing, so N concurrent requests on a cold client issue N refreshes. Microsoft persists whichever rotated refresh_token arrives via onRefreshTokenRotated, so concurrent refreshes race on which token is stored (provider-side consequence INFERRED). Clients are built per request in the cloud runtime, so in-process coalescing would not cover cross-request or cross-replica races.
findings.recommendation: Coalesce refreshes behind a shared promise as LinkedIn does; for hosted deployments serialize rotated-token persistence with select ... for update on private.provider_credentials.

findings.title: Non-atomic file writes in local-mode stores; no report index file exists
findings.description: Pending, findings and credential stores write JSON directly to the final path (no temp+rename), so a reader racing a writer can see truncated JSON and get a parse error instead of a clean not-found. Audit appendFile lines may exceed PIPE_BUF when details are large and could interleave across processes (INFERRED). The 'report index file' hazard named in the workstream does not apply: engine reports and artifacts write one file per id and there is no shared index.
findings.recommendation: Write to a temp file and rename; keep audit lines short or guard with a lock file.

findings.title: In-memory engine profile lacks locks in approval and dedupe stores
findings.description: InMemoryProposalRepository has a Lock but InMemoryApprovalRepository.mark_used and InMemoryDedupeStore.seen are check-then-act. Used only when DATABASE_URL is unset (docstring says not a production profile); with Postgres the atomic SQL stores are used. The contract race test still passes because the locked proposal CAS catches the loser first.

findings.title: Pending-operation consumption is not atomic: concurrent or retried applies execute the provider write twice
evidence: harness E2/E3/E4: node f7-harness.mjs exit 0 — applyWrite called twice after audit/delete failure and under concurrent apply
findings.description: apply() runs get → applyWrite → audit.append → pending.delete with no claim on the row; PostgresPendingStore.get is a plain select and delete an unconditional update. Two concurrent approvals both execute the provider write; a Postgres failure after the provider write leaves the row active so a retry writes again. Bridge-mapped tools are 'update' kind (idempotent values), but the dashboard apply route applies any active pending row of the organization including MCP/REST-created 'create' operations, where a repeat creates a duplicate budgeted campaign.
findings.recommendation: Claim the row before the provider call (update ... where consumed_at is null returning), record apply_started/applied/apply_failed states, pass provider idempotency keys, and add tests for concurrent apply and post-write store failures.

findings.title: An executed provider write can leave no 'applied' audit event
evidence: harness E2: audit ['validated'] only after a successful applyWrite
findings.description: If audit.append fails after applyWrite succeeds, the platform changed but the audit log shows only 'validated', the pending row stays active, the route returns a masked 500 and no outcome is marked.
findings.recommendation: Persist an apply_started marker before the provider call and the outcome after it on the pending row itself; surface an 'outcome unknown' state in the UI.

findings.title: Infrastructure failures at preview are recorded and reported to the engine as policy rejections
evidence: scratch F3: outcome rejected_by_policy, code ERROR, engine told 'adport refused the preview (ERROR)'
harness E5: orphan pending row with no validated audit event
findings.description: Any thrown error inside the preview (e.g. Postgres failure in the audit insert) becomes status rejected_by_policy in provenance, an 'Engine proposal refused' audit note, and a 'refused' hand-off message to the engine thread; in the E5 variant an approvable pending row also exists with no provenance link.
findings.recommendation: Branch on AdportError codes; record a distinct 'error' status, do not tell the engine it was refused, return 503; add a throwing-audit-store test.

findings.title: Hand-off ordering: failure after preview leaves an approvable row, an untold engine, and a re-bridge of the same proposal next turn
evidence: scratch F1/F2: pending row exists, rejectOnEngine never called
probe S2: next turn returns same proposal awaiting_approval with interrupted=False
findings.description: record()/note() failures after a successful preview leave a pending row, skip the engine hand-off, and return 500. The engine attaches the still-awaiting proposal to the next turn; assistant.ts bridges on state alone and creates a second pending row; the provenance upsert re-points to the new row so the older row stays approvable without provenance. End-to-end chain across turns with a live DB was inferred, components verified at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Dedupe on (proposal_id, revision)/payload_digest before previewing; wrap record+note in one transaction with compensation; bridge only when interrupted is true or the proposal is newer than the last user message.

findings.title: Engine timeout: client aborts at 240 s but the engine keeps running; orphaned proposal has no TTL and resurfaces later
evidence: probe S2/S3: orphan still awaiting_approval after two further turns and attached to outcomes
findings.description: On abort the user gets a masked 500 and a consumed rate-limit token; the engine finishes later (continuation after client abort is inferred from the absence of cancellation handling). Live-mode budget (120 s per call, SDK and middleware retries, 40 calls) can legitimately exceed 240 s. The resulting proposal has no expiry and is previewed on the next turn as if freshly requested. No test covers AbortError or assistant.ts.
findings.recommendation: Make chat turns asynchronous or align budgets; track in-flight turns; bridge only fresh/interrupted proposals; add an engine-side sweep that rejects stale awaiting proposals.

findings.title: The 'engine not reachable' message can never reach the user; engine 4xx detail can
findings.description: apiError replaces every >=500 message with 'Internal server error.', so the crafted 503 text is dead code, while engine 401/404/409 detail is forwarded verbatim to the browser.
findings.recommendation: Return a dedicated error code body for engine unavailability and map engine 4xx to fixed product messages.

findings.title: Apply and reject routes are multi-statement without a transaction
findings.description: Postgres failing between delete/recordAudit/markPendingOutcome leaves a consumed row with no rejected audit event, or an applied operation whose provenance stays 'pending'. No test covers partial states.
findings.recommendation: Wrap consume + audit + provenance update in one db().begin; derive provenance status from the pending row.

findings.title: Provenance rows are never marked 'expired'
evidence: rg "'expired'" platform/apps/cloud/app platform/apps/cloud/lib => no caller of markPendingOutcome(...,'expired')
findings.description: Expiry is applied to pending_operations by sweep/filter but markting_engine_proposals.status stays 'pending' forever for unreviewed operations.
findings.recommendation: Derive status at read time or add the transition to the sweep.

findings.title: Stripe webhook: check-then-insert idempotency and no event ordering guard
findings.description: Retries after a processing failure work (non-2xx → Stripe retries, inferred). Concurrent duplicate deliveries both pass the pre-check; out-of-order subscription.updated deliveries during retries can regress plan/status and disable ad accounts under the wrong cap; processing errors are reported as 400 'Invalid Stripe webhook.' indistinguishable from signature failures.
findings.recommendation: Claim the event id first and roll back on failure; compare event.created / subscription state monotonically; return 500 for processing errors.

findings.title: Supabase Auth outage presents as 'Authentication required.' (401) everywhere
findings.description: Any getUser error is treated as no session; dashboard users are told they are logged out during an outage. Fail-closed, but misleading, with no retry/backoff and no test. SDK returning error objects rather than throwing is inferred.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish retryable fetch errors from missing sessions and return 503 with a clear message.

findings.title: Engine: duplicate /reject is an unhandled 500; a late reject resumes whichever interrupt is current
evidence: probe S6: duplicate reject → 500; probe S4: late reject of orphan injected a reject decision into the newer proposal's interrupt
findings.description: Bridge retries of the hand-off produce engine tracebacks; rejecting an orphan while a newer proposal awaits review resolves the newer proposal's interrupt. Engine cannot write, so impact is logs/UX.
findings.recommendation: Catch InvalidTransition → 409; resume only when the current interrupt belongs to the rejected proposal.

findings.title: Apply/reject look the row up in a 200-row window
findings.description: listPendingOperations(org, 200).find(id) returns 404 for older rows when more than 200 are active.
findings.recommendation: Select the row by id and organization directly.

findings.title: No failure-injection test coverage for timeouts, store failures, concurrency, webhook retries, or auth outage
findings.description: Existing suites pass (24 + 10 + 7) but exercise none of the failure modes enumerated in F7-01..F7-10; the in-memory stores already present make these tests cheap.
findings.recommendation: Add throwing-store, concurrent-apply, AbortError, record()-failure, Stripe duplicate/out-of-order and Supabase network-error tests.

key_findings: Pending-row consumption is not atomic: concurrent approvals or a Postgres failure after the provider write execute the ad-platform write twice (harness E2-E4; engine.ts:90-124, repository.ts:383-418); dashboard apply can reach non-idempotent MCP-created 'create' rows.
A successful provider write can leave only a 'validated' audit event and an active pending row (harness E2).

Bridge treats any infra error at preview as rejected_by_policy and tells the engine 'adport refused' (scratch F3, bridge.ts:76-83); record()/note() failures leave approvable rows with the engine never told (F1/F2).

Engine attaches the latest awaiting proposal to every turn (runner.py:134); after a client timeout or a hand-off failure the same proposal is re-bridged a turn later, creating duplicate pending rows and re-pointing provenance (probe S2, assistant.ts:51, repository.ts:84-86).

Client timeout 240 s vs engine live budget (120 s x retries x up to 40 calls) is a design mismatch; orphaned proposals have no TTL (probe S3); the 'engine not reachable' message is dead code due to apiError masking (http.ts:26-28).
Apply/reject routes and the bridge run multi-statement sequences without transactions; provenance never reaches 'expired'.
Stripe webhook idempotency is check-then-insert with no ordering guard; out-of-order retries can regress plan and disable ad accounts (billing.ts:56-137).
Duplicate engine /reject is an unhandled 500 and a late reject resumes the thread's current interrupt (probe S4/S6), confirming ARCHITECTURE.md:824.

findings.title: Engine report runs are global, not per-organization; any signed-in user lists and downloads every run
findings.description: GET /api/reports/engine validates a session then returns engineClient().listReports() with no org filter; the file route proxies any rpt_*/art_* file after a session check only. One shared index and one shared MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN mean org A's runs appear in org B's list and are downloadable. Currently fixture data (G2-01) so no tenant leak today; becomes P0 cross-tenant the moment the engine sees real data.
findings.recommendation: Namespace runs by organization on the adport side (store run ids keyed by org, filter listReports, refuse downloads for ids the org does not own) or pass an org identifier to /reports/run and index per org.

findings.title: Overview ROAS tile is always 0x because conversion_value is never requested
findings.description: readReport requests metrics ['spend','impressions','clicks','conversions','roas'] but live-data.tsx computes blended ROAS from row.metrics.conversion_value, which providers never return because they project to requested metrics only. The headline ROAS is structurally 0 while the per-row ROAS column shows real values; the footer 'Conversion value / spend' describes a computation that cannot succeed.
findings.recommendation: Request conversion_value (or use summary.groups[].metrics.roas from the report tool) or remove the tile until it can be computed honestly.

findings.title: Overview sums spend and ROAS across currencies and discards the tool's currency-separated summary
findings.description: A single reduce over all rows ignores row.currency; the report tool's summary (per-currency totals, spend-weighted ROAS) is destructured away in reads.ts even though the tool description says never combine currencies. Neither Overview nor Reports table has a currency column. A SAR + USD tenant sees one meaningless spend number.
findings.recommendation: Render summary.groups as one tile group per currency using the existing formatMoney helper; add a currency column to both tables.

findings.title: Approval row not actionable: summary only, no before/after, deltas, risk or plans; reject has no reason field
findings.description: The row shows preview.summary, the pending id, and engine reason sliced to 160 chars. preview.changes/coercions/budgetDeltas/serverValidated and engine before/after/risk/risk_flags/measurement_plan/reversal_plan are loaded but never rendered. Apply confirmation is a generic window.confirm; reject posts {organizationId} only although the API accepts and audits a 300-char reason. Expiry is an absolute UTC timestamp with a 15-minute default TTL. The requester's BridgeCard in the Assistant shows more than the approver's page.
findings.recommendation: Expand each row with changes, budgetDeltas (before -> after, % delta, currency), coercions, serverValidated, engine risk/plans, full reason, requester identity, relative expiry; add reject-reason input; replace window.confirm with inline confirmation restating the change.

Nothing the AI media buyer itself says is Arabic: engine/instructions.md has no language clause, no locale is forwarded, the demo engine replies in English, reports hard-code lang=en, and provider ids/audit summaries/errors are English inside Arabic pages.

G5.scope: Cloud dashboard information architecture: nav grouping (components/nav.tsx), shell layout, page headers/cards/tables across all 8 primary + 4 utility routes, where KPIs live (live-data.tsx), whether the Assistant is the hub, and a proposed module IA (Ask AI, Morning Brief, Account Health, Opportunities, Creative Intelligence, Budget Optimizer, Alerts, Experiments, Recommendations, Approvals, Decision History, Outcome Tracking) mapped to platform + engine code.

findings.title: Findings is a primary nav module with no producer in the codebase
evidence: grep -rn '\.save(' over findings across platform/ and services/ => no caller (exit 0, empty)
findings.description: Findings occupies one of eight primary nav slots and the page renders an audit-findings table, claiming the capability. PostgresFindingsStore.save (the only insert into public.findings, repository.ts:477) is never called anywhere in platform/ or services/; the two runtime builders only construct the store. So in a normal deployment the page is permanently empty.
findings.recommendation: Wire a producer (engine audit pass or a cloud job calling PostgresFindingsStore.save) or demote Findings out of primary nav until populated; document and verify the write path if it is intended to be engine-produced.
findings.failure_scenario: A user clicks Findings (primary nav); because no code ever writes a finding, the page shows the empty state forever, indistinguishable from 'all healthy'.

findings.title: Overview, not the Assistant, is the hub; the AI action surface is secondary
findings.description: The product is positioned as an AI media buyer, but the landing surface is a passive normalized-read dashboard and the Assistant (the only surface that turns intent into an approvable action) is a peer nav link #2 with no shell presence, no command bar, and no entry point from Overview.
findings.recommendation: Make Ask AI the hub: persistent composer/command bar in the shell or on Overview, with dashboard surfaces deep-linking into the Assistant.
findings.failure_scenario: A first-time user lands on Overview, sees only read-only tables and counts, and never discovers that the Assistant can propose and apply changes.

findings.title: KPIs live in one place only, computed client-side, with no per-account or trend context
findings.description: The only KPI row in the app (Spend/Clicks/Conversions/ROAS) is on Overview over a fixed 7-day window; totals and ROAS are summed/divided in the browser rather than by the engine's deterministic compute. No period-over-period delta, no per-account breakdown, no trend, and no KPIs on any other page.
findings.recommendation: Add period-over-period deltas (engine compare_periods already produces them), compute ROAS server-side for parity with engine reports, and add a per-account health rollup.
findings.failure_scenario: A buyer cannot tell whether this week's ROAS is up or down vs last week, nor which account drives the headline number, without reading the 12-row table.

findings.title: Overview campaign table and Reports campaign table are near-duplicates differing only by window
findings.description: Overview 'Campaign activity' (7d) and Reports 'Campaigns' (30d) render essentially the same entity table with identical Provider/status rendering, differing only by window and one Impressions column. The window is baked into the route; there is no single campaign explorer with a window selector.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate into one campaign/entity explorer with a window control and drill-down; keep Overview as a summarized brief and reserve Reports for the engine's deterministic deliverables.
findings.failure_scenario: Users must learn two near-identical screens (Overview=7d, Reports=30d) instead of choosing a window once, and the two tables drift (Overview has ROAS but no Impressions).

findings.title: No decision/outcome layer: applied changes are logged as events but never tracked for effect
findings.description: The system proposes, approves, and logs changes (audit validated/applied/rejected), but nothing links an applied change to its subsequent performance delta. Decision History exists only implicitly as the event-centric Audit log; Outcome Tracking is absent (engine 'outcome' is RunOutcome run plumbing, not performance attribution).
findings.recommendation: Add a decision-centric history keyed on applied operations (join audit 'applied' events to the originating proposal) plus an Outcome Tracking surface that re-reads affected entities post-change via compare_periods.
findings.failure_scenario: After the agent applies a budget change, the user has no view of what it did to spend/CPA/ROAS, so cannot build trust in or measure the agent's value.

key_findings: Findings is a primary nav module (nav.tsx:32) backed by a store whose save() is never called anywhere in platform/ or services/ — a shipped primary feature that is permanently empty (P2, VERIFIED_CODE).
The Assistant (the only action-producing surface) is nav link #2 with no shell presence; Overview, a passive read dashboard, is the hub — contradicting the 'AI media buyer' positioning.
KPIs (Spend/Clicks/Conversions/ROAS) exist only on Overview, over a fixed 7d window, computed client-side, with no deltas, per-account view, or trend.
Overview 'Campaign activity' (7d) and Reports 'Campaigns' (30d) are near-duplicate tables; no unified campaign explorer with a window selector.

Of the 12 proposed IA modules, only Approvals (strong) and Ask AI (limited) fully exist; Morning Brief, Opportunities, Creative Intelligence, Alerts, Experiments, Outcome Tracking are MISSING; Account Health, Recommendations, Decision History are PARTIAL.
No decision/outcome loop: applied changes are logged as audit events but never attributed to a performance delta.
Current primary nav mixes the work loop with workspace config; a cleaner split is a loop rail (Ask AI, Brief, Health, Opportunities, Approvals, Decisions/Outcomes) + Analyze + Settings groups.

G5.disagreements: README.md positions the product as an 'AI media buyer', but the implemented IA defaults to a passive read dashboard (app/dashboard/page.tsx) with the agentic loop buried as nav link #2 and absent from the shell (G5-02). The Findings nav entry and page imply an active audit-findings capability (nav.tsx:32, findings/page.tsx), contradicted by the complete absence of any save() caller (G5-01). Conversely, the assistant page copy claiming every suggested change 'becomes a previewed operation on the Approvals page' is VERIFIED_CODE-accurate (assistant.ts:60-75) — a doc/code agreement worth noting as a strength.
G5.not_verified: Whether public.findings is populated out-of-band (infra/ SQL seed, migration, or an external cron/service outside platform/ and services/) — I confirmed no in-repo platform caller of save() but did not audit infra/ SQL exhaustively; if such a producer exists, G5-01 softens to P3/GAP. No runtime rendering was performed (no VERIFIED_RUNTIME); all layout/hierarchy claims are from source + globals.css reads. The engine's full tool surface beyond sampled files was not read line-by-line; MISSING module verdicts rest on targeted grep, so a capability under an unexpected name could exist. Did not read other agents' reports (not a lead/reviewer).

findings.title: Default free plan makes the write-preview promise impossible; onboarding never discloses it
findings.description: Every new signup defaults to reader/Free (migration default 'reader'). Reader strips tools:write (plans.ts:103); the dry-run preview is the first half of the same readOnly:false write tool (write.ts:38,52), so a Free user cannot even preview. Onboarding welcome bullet pointPreview and agent tipPreview promise 'every write requires an exact preview' with no plan/upgrade context anywhere in the flow. REST tool route and dashboard apply return a raw 'API key lacks required scope: tools:write' 403; only the MCP path degrades gracefully to a PLAN_LIMIT message, and only when grantedScopes still has tools:write.
findings.recommendation: Add a plan/limits panel to onboarding stating Free is read-only and writes need Operator+, with an upgrade link; return the same structured PLAN_LIMIT message on the REST /api/v1/tools and approvals apply paths that the MCP path already produces.

findings.title: No organization switcher; invited members can never reach the workspace they were invited to
findings.description: requireDashboardTenant selects the membership ordered by created_at asc limit 1. A user invited via inviteUserByEmail already has (or is given at signup, via the handle_new_user personal-org trigger) a personal org older than the invited membership, so they always land in their own empty personal org. There is no org switcher in nav/shell and no route reads a chosen org id. This makes the Agency clientWorkspaces/team feature unreachable for invitees.
findings.recommendation: Add an organization selector that persists the active org (cookie/session), or route a freshly-invited user to the inviting org on first login.

findings.title: Provider cards have no 'awaiting app approval' state; opaque 'Unavailable' is a silent dead-end and contradicts docs
findings.description: The only unavailable state is 'Unavailable'/'غير متاح'. It conflates not-configured, rollout-gated, and synthetic-reviewer suppression, and when a provider is unavailable AND unconnected the Actions column renders nothing (provider-connections.tsx:89) so the user gets no button and no reason. On a deployment with provider OAuth env unset (an un-met production gate per README/TODO) every card is Unavailable and a new user can connect nothing. docs/snapchat-live-checklist.md:17 and PHASE0-REPORT reference card copy '...approval' that does not exist in code.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish provider states (not-configured/pending-review/rollout-gated/ready) with specific copy and a disabled card + tooltip reason; fix or remove the doc references to the non-existent approval copy.

findings.title: Two separate 'accounts' surfaces; the account picker sits outside the onboarding stepper
findings.description: The onboarding accounts step renders AccountAccessManager (enable/disable already-added accounts, capped by plan maxActiveAccounts=3 free). Choosing which discovered accounts to add is a separate /account-selection page the OAuth callback always redirects to, outside the onboarding progress UI, then returns to /onboarding. The add-vs-enable distinction is under-explained and there is no in-flow path from the onboarding accounts step to the picker if selection is pending (that link lives on Connections).
findings.recommendation: Embed the account picker as a sub-step within the onboarding shell with the progress indicator intact, and clearly sequence 'add' then 'enable for agent'.

findings.title: Arabic-first first-run lacks SAR/VAT pricing, plan disclosure, and guided activation
findings.description: The i18n/RTL layer is strong (DEFAULT_LOCALE=ar, dir=rtl, fully bilingual onboarding/agents messages). What is missing for a Saudi/MENA media buyer is commercial localization (prices are EUR-only monthlyPriceEur/annualPriceEur, no SAR/VAT), no plan/pricing step in onboarding, and no guided first task beyond a single safePromptText string or seeded sample data on the real (non-demo) path.
findings.recommendation: Localize currency (SAR) and VAT, add an up-front plan/limits step, and add a guided first-report/first-analysis action on a connected account.

findings.title: Vendored 'Adport' branding and hardcoded English title leak through the Arabic-first product
findings.description: The onboarding page metadata title is hardcoded English 'Set up Adport' (not localized) and onboarding copy references the upstream 'Adport' brand in both locales, on the most brand-sensitive first-run screen of the Arabic-first 'markting' product.
findings.recommendation: Replace with the product brand and localize the metadata title through the i18n layer.

key_findings: Default plan for every new signup is reader/Free, which strips tools:write and therefore makes the write-preview (the onboarding's headline safety promise) impossible; onboarding never discloses the plan or an upgrade path (G4-01).

No organization switcher: requireDashboardTenant always picks the oldest membership, so invited team/agency members land in their own personal org and can never reach the workspace they were invited to (G4-02).
Provider cards have no 'awaiting app approval' state the docs claim; the single opaque 'Unavailable' renders no button and no reason, a silent connect-step dead-end when OAuth env is unset (G4-03).
Account 'add' (separate /account-selection page) and 'enable for agent' (onboarding accounts step) are two surfaces; the picker is outside the onboarding progress UI (G4-04).
Arabic/RTL is correctly implemented, but the commercial first-run is EUR-only with no SAR/VAT, no plan step, and no guided activation for a MENA buyer (G4-05).
Onboarding leaks the upstream 'Adport' brand and a hardcoded English page title (G4-06).
Onboarding state persistence, admin gating, step validation, and account-selection are functional and covered by 57 passing tests.
G4.disagreements: docs/snapchat-live-checklist.md:17 and docs/PHASE0-REPORT.md tell operators to watch for provider-card copy '...approval'; no such UI string exists — the only unavailable state is 'Unavailable'/'غير متاح' (connections.ts:20,57). Onboarding's own pointPreview (onboarding.ts:15) and tipPreview (agents.ts:50) promise 'every write requires an exact preview', which the default reader plan cannot deliver (plans.ts:25,103; write.ts:38). The team invite UI (team-members.tsx, api/members/route.ts) implies a working shared workspace, but dashboard.ts:38-41 makes the invited org unreachable for the invitee.
G4.not_verified: End-to-end runtime of the OAuth->popup->account-selection->onboarding round-trip (traced via code + unit tests, not executed against a live Supabase/provider stack; VERIFIED_CODE not VERIFIED_RUNTIME). The exact 403 body an agent sees on a Free-plan write over MCP vs REST (read from code, not captured from a running server). The membership-timestamp ordering behind the invitee-lands-in-personal-org claim (inferred from the handle_new_user trigger + invite insert order; strongly implied, not executed). Full cloud test suite, typecheck, and build were not run; only the three onboarding-adjacent test files (57 tests, exit 0).

G6.scope: Enterprise readiness of the markting-ai cloud app: RBAC (owner/admin/member/viewer) definition and enforcement, approval workflows, audit log capture/export/retention, API key & MCP access and scopes, SSO/MFA/SCIM, data retention, organization hierarchy and agency client workspaces, and offboarding/deletion.

findings.title: RBAC is a coarse flat 4-role model; no custom roles or per-account/provider scoping
findings.description: Roles are a hard-coded enum (owner/admin/member/viewer) enforced by ad-hoc includes() checks scattered across call sites. No permission matrix, no custom roles, no per-connection/per-ad-account scoping, no teams/groups. member differs from viewer essentially only in being able to reject a pending op.
findings.recommendation: Introduce resource-scoped permissions (per connection/ad-account), a declarative permission matrix, and optional custom roles.

findings.title: Approval workflow is single-approver only; no multi-step/quorum/SLA/delegation, and API/MCP writes have no second approver
findings.description: Dashboard approval requires one owner/admin; the only separation-of-duties control (creator cannot approve) is bypassable via MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL. No sequential/multi-step approval, no N-of-M quorum, no budget-threshold tiers, no SLA/escalation (pending ops only expire via pending_ttl_minutes), no delegation. The REST/MCP write path executes writes directly under a single credential with no human approval at all.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable approval policies (threshold, N-of-M, role-targeted), SLA/escalation, delegation, and an option to force API/MCP writes through the pending-approval queue.

findings.title: 'Separate client workspaces' is a paid, advertised feature that is not implemented
findings.description: The clientWorkspaces plan flag (agency & enterprise) is sold in the billing UI as 'Separate client workspaces' but is consumed only to render a feature bullet. No code or schema partitions an organization into per-client workspaces/sub-accounts; the only isolation unit is the flat organization. Agencies (the named target market) cannot segregate clients.
findings.recommendation: Implement workspace partitioning (parent org + child workspaces with scoped connections, billing roll-up, and workspace-scoped roles) or remove the feature claim from paid tiers until shipped.

findings.title: No enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC) or SCIM despite Enterprise tier advertising 'Includes SSO'
findings.description: Authentication is Supabase email/password plus google/github social OAuth only. No SAML/enterprise OIDC IdP, no SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning, no domain auto-join; membership is manual invite only. Contradicts the sold Enterprise 'Includes SSO' feature.
findings.recommendation: Add SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM provisioning gated behind the enterprise entitlement.

findings.title: Audit log cannot be exported; UI is capped, unfiltered, and hides actor identity
findings.description: The audit view renders only the latest 150 events with no export (CSV/JSON/API), no date/actor/provider filters, no pagination, and shows actor only as generic member/api-key/system rather than a person/email. No audit-export route exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a paginated, filterable audit view, an export API, SIEM streaming, and resolved actor identity.

findings.title: Audit trail is non-durable: hard-deleted by retention cron, actor nulled on user delete, no IP/user-agent
findings.description: audit_events has actor_user_id ON DELETE SET NULL and no IP/user-agent columns. private.apply_data_retention() hard-deletes audit_events older than data_retention_days (default 30) daily via pg_cron, with no archival or immutable export. Deleting a user erases their audit attribution. Fails tamper-evident/long-retention/attributable audit expectations.
findings.recommendation: Capture IP/user-agent, preserve actor identity, and archive audit events to immutable/WORM storage before retention purge.

findings.title: API keys never expire, are org-wide, and support only two coarse scopes
findings.description: createApiKey never sets expires_at (keys never expire; no rotation/TTL). Scopes are limited to tools:read/tools:write with no per-account/provider restriction; keys are org-wide. authenticateApiKey returns no role, so key write access is governed by plan only.
findings.recommendation: Default/forced key expiry and rotation reminders; resource-scoped key scopes.

findings.title: MFA is disabled in configuration; no org-level MFA enforcement
findings.description: The committed Supabase config disables TOTP (enroll/verify=false) and phone MFA; WebAuthn is commented out. There is no application-level requirement for org members to use MFA. A hosted Supabase project could re-enable factors, so production state is not fully verified.
findings.recommendation: Enable TOTP/WebAuthn and add an org policy to require MFA with step-up on apply/delete.

findings.title: No organization hierarchy / teams / groups / consolidated billing
findings.description: Tenancy is a single flat level: flat organizations (no parent_id), flat memberships, per-org subscription. Multi-brand enterprises/agencies must create independent orgs with duplicated connections, separate billing, and no cross-org role, parent-admin visibility, or consolidated invoicing.
findings.recommendation: Add an org hierarchy (parent account to workspaces/teams), cross-org admin roles, and roll-up billing.

findings.title: Offboarding/deletion is synchronous, revokes only Google at the IdP, ignores the designed deletion lifecycle, and has no data export
findings.description: Org deletion is owner-only and synchronous: it revokes only the Google provider grant, then hard-deletes the organization; other providers' external OAuth grants are not revoked (DB rows cascade only). The deletion_requests table and deletion_status lifecycle are designed but unused. No GDPR/DSAR data-export before deletion.
findings.recommendation: Revoke all provider grants on deletion, drive deletion through the tracked deletion_requests lifecycle, and offer a pre-deletion data export.

key_findings: RBAC is a coarse, flat 4-role enum enforced by scattered includes() checks; no custom roles, no per-account/provider scoping, no teams (P2).
Approval is single-approver only — no multi-step/quorum/SLA/delegation — and the REST/MCP write path has no second-approver at all; the one SoD check is env-flag-bypassable (P2).
'Separate client workspaces' is sold on Agency/Enterprise plans but is entirely unimplemented — the flag is only a billing bullet; tenancy is a flat org (P1).
No enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC) or SCIM despite Enterprise copy claiming 'Includes SSO'; only Supabase social + password (P2).
Audit log has no export, caps at 150 rows, lacks filters, and hides actor identity; events are hard-deleted by a retention cron with no archival and lose attribution on user delete (P2 x2).
MFA (TOTP/phone) is disabled in the committed Supabase config and there is no org-level MFA enforcement (P2).

No org hierarchy/consolidated billing; API keys never expire and are org-wide with only read/write scopes; deletion revokes only Google and skips the designed deletion lifecycle and data export (P3 x3).
G6.disagreements: Billing Enterprise copy 'Includes SSO … SLA …' (lib/i18n/messages/billing.ts:58) contradicts code: no SSO/SAML/OIDC (login/actions.ts:8) and no approval SLA/escalation logic. 'Separate client workspaces' advertised for Agency/Enterprise (billing.ts:53, plans.ts:38/42) is unimplemented — the flag is read only to render a billing bullet (billing/page.tsx:95). Retention is upsold as 'longer audit history' (support.ts:38) but the retention cron hard-deletes audit events with no archival (apply_data_retention), so history is destroyed rather than preserved.
G6.not_verified: Runtime behavior of approval/deletion/REST routes (VERIFIED_CODE only — no server executed). Whether the hosted Supabase project overrides config.toml to enable MFA/SSO in production (committed config shows disabled; DOCUMENTED_ONLY for prod). Whether every markting-bridge agent write path forces the pending-approval queue vs. allowing direct apply — the dashboard apply/reject routes and the REST v1/tools direct path were verified, but not every bridge entry point was traced. No tests were run for this workstream.

findings.title: Cloud build context has no .dockerignore; gitignored .env.local secrets and 577MB node_modules enter the Docker build
findings.description: cloud.Dockerfile does `COPY . .` from context ./platform with no .dockerignore, so a developer's gitignored apps/cloud/.env.local secrets and 577MB of host node_modules/.turbo/.git are pulled into the build-stage layer. next build auto-loads .env.local (NEXT_PUBLIC_* inlined into client bundle; build-time secrets can override intended runtime config). Final image is multi-stage so residual final-image reach is inferred, but build-layer secret leak and build bloat are verified.
findings.recommendation: Add platform/.dockerignore excluding node_modules, .next, .turbo, coverage, .git, **/.env, **/.env.* (keep !**/.env.example), website, docs, supabase; confirm .env.local is not traced into .next/standalone.

findings.title: Engine container runs as root (no USER directive)
findings.description: The engine service (runs serve_demo.py, writes kill-switch + workspace) executes as UID 0. The cloud image drops to node; the engine image does not. Low impact in localhost demo, P2 in a hardened/production deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create and switch to a non-root user in engine/Dockerfile, chown /app/workspace.

findings.title: Base images tag-pinned, not digest-pinned
findings.description: node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.13-slim, postgres:16-alpine all tag-only, no @sha256 digest. Rebuilds not reproducible and exposed to tag mutation.
findings.recommendation: Pin base images to digests with a controlled bump/scan process.

findings.title: Whole root .env injected into engine, giving it cloud/Stripe/Supabase secrets it never uses
evidence: rendered `docker compose config` engine env includes SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, ADPORT_API_KEY_PEPPER, ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY, ADPORT_MCP_OAUTH_SIGNING_KEY
findings.description: Both services load the same full .env; the engine needs only DATABASE_URL, PAID_MEDIA_* and MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN yet receives every cloud/billing/DB secret, widening blast radius. Mitigated (not removed) by environment: overrides of safety vars and serve_demo.py fail-closed boot assertions.
findings.recommendation: Give the engine an explicit minimal environment or an engine-scoped env file instead of env_file: .env.

findings.title: Cloud image builds Next.js twice
findings.description: `pnpm build` (turbo) already builds the cloud app, then `build:standalone` runs `next build` a second time. Inefficiency only; standalone recipe is otherwise correct (prepare-standalone.mjs nests server at .next/standalone/apps/cloud/server.js, matching CMD).
findings.recommendation: Build only workspace deps then a single standalone build, or drop the first pnpm build.

findings.title: No reverse proxy / TLS in front of cloud
findings.description: Stack is localhost HTTP only; deliberate for the demo but no TLS/HSTS/edge exists for any non-local deployment. Secure-cookie/OAuth-over-HTTPS flows will not work behind nothing. GAP, not a demo defect.
findings.recommendation: Document/add a TLS reverse proxy for shared/production deployments.

findings.title: Primary DB (Supabase) is outside compose; stack is not self-contained and cloud is not gated on DB readiness
findings.description: `docker compose up` alone does not produce a working system: Supabase must be started via the Supabase CLI on the host and reached via host.docker.internal, and cloud has no dependency/health gate on Supabase readiness so it can boot before migrations apply. Rationale (auth.users, pg_cron, adport_backend role) is legitimate but result is non-self-contained orchestration split across make+CLI+compose.
findings.recommendation: For production use managed Supabase/Postgres with migration gating; document that compose alone is not the full stack.

findings.title: No healthcheck for the cloud service
findings.description: Nothing verifies the cloud app is serving; restart: unless-stopped will not restart a hung-but-alive process and no dependent waits on cloud health.
findings.recommendation: Add a cloud healthcheck hitting a Next route or /api/health.

findings.title: Engine HEALTHCHECK lacks start-period tuning
findings.description: Engine boot runs Postgres checkpointer setup and graph assembly; with no start_period early checks count toward failure. 12x10s (~120s) buffer makes flapping unlikely but a start_period would be correct.
findings.recommendation: Add start_period (~20-30s).

findings.title: Committed __pycache__/*.pyc under bind-mounted demo service
findings.description: Stale cpython-311 bytecode is tracked and read-only-mounted into a python:3.13 container. Unused (version mismatch) and read-only so harmless at runtime; committed build residue only.
findings.recommendation: Gitignore __pycache__/ and .pytest_cache/ under services/.

key_findings: docker compose config is valid (exit 0) only once a root .env exists; it fails closed when MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN is unset — the token var uses ${VAR:?}.

P1: cloud build context has NO platform/.dockerignore, so `COPY . .` pulls a gitignored apps/cloud/.env.local (SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, ADPORT encryption/pepper/signing keys) and 577MB node_modules into the Docker build layer; next build also auto-loads .env.local.
Engine container runs as root (no USER); only the cloud image drops to USER node.
No base image is digest-pinned (node:22, python:3.13, postgres:16-alpine all tag-only).

Whole root .env is injected into the engine via env_file, handing it cloud/Stripe/Supabase secrets it never uses (blast-radius); mitigated by environment overrides + serve_demo.py fail-closed boot checks.
Production gaps: no reverse proxy/TLS, and Supabase (the primary DB) lives outside compose with cloud not gated on DB readiness, so `docker compose up` alone is not a working stack.
Safety strengths verified: ports bound to 127.0.0.1 only, engine/engine-db unpublished, read-only code/skill mounts, engine writes forced off via environment overrides that beat env_file.
H1.disagreements: docker-compose.yml:35 calls the engine image 'Upstream image, unchanged' — true for the image build but misleading at runtime: safety (proposal-only provider + kill switch) comes from the compose `command` running services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py (serve_demo.py:69-81,173-180) and the environment overrides, NOT from the image, which still defaults to `paid-media-agent serve`. The stock image is not itself proposal-only. Also, Makefile/.env.example imply `make env` + `make up` yields a complete stack, but compose alone (a) fails even `config` without a root .env (verified exit 1) and (b) is not a working system without the separate Supabase CLI step (H1-07).
H1.not_verified: Image builds/up are blocked by the sandbox (network) and were not retried per task rules, so no VERIFIED_RUNTIME: actual `docker compose build`/`up`, whether next build traces .env.local into .next/standalone (final-image reach of the H1-01 leak is INFERRED), real root execution in the engine container, healthcheck timing under real boot, and that `python` resolves to /app/.venv/bin/python at runtime (INFERRED from engine/Dockerfile:19 PATH).

findings.title: Ad-platform apply (write) produces no audit event, structured log, or metric
findings.description: The apply route calls applyPending then markPendingOutcome('applied') but never recordAudit; the reject route does record audit. The real ad-account mutation leaves only a pending_operations status flag, with no audit_events row, no structured log, and no success/failure metric. On failure, applyPending throws into apiError which only console.error's for >=500 and markPendingOutcome is skipped, leaving the row silently 'pending'.
findings.recommendation: Record an audit_events row and structured log (actor, org, pendingId, tool, account, outcome, latency, error class) on both success and failure of apply; add apply success/failure counters and alert on elevated failure rate.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner applies a budget change; the provider write fails. apiError returns the error, no audit row is written, markPendingOutcome('applied') never runs, no alert fires. Operators cannot tell the apply was attempted or that it failed.
findings.short_summary: Apply path writes no audit event, log, or metric

findings.title: No metrics anywhere: requests, engine runs, or LLM token/cost
findings.description: Tree-wide search finds no prometheus/opentelemetry/statsd/datadog instrumentation and no metrics dependency in either package manifest. No request latency/count/error metric, no engine run metric, and no LLM token or cost metric despite an LLM-driven agent. 'metrics' appears only as ad-performance UI fields.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal metrics layer: request count/latency/error by route+status; engine run count/duration/outcome; apply success/failure; per-org LLM prompt/completion tokens and estimated cost (at least as structured events if no backend chosen).
findings.failure_scenario: Model cost or latency regresses, or a tenant drives runaway spend; there is no counter, timer, or log to detect it, so the first signal is a bill or a user complaint.
findings.short_summary: Zero metrics/telemetry in cloud or engine

findings.title: Engine logging is unstructured plaintext without correlation/tenant ids and barely used
findings.description: logging.basicConfig uses a human-readable format '%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s' with no JSON and no org/thread/proposal/caller/trace ids. Only 5 logger call sites exist in the entire engine src; the FastAPI write/preview/apply/report handlers emit essentially no application logs.
findings.recommendation: Adopt structured JSON logging with request-scoped trace ids and org/thread/proposal/caller fields; log at the boundaries of every write/preview/apply/report with outcome and duration.
findings.failure_scenario: A write pipeline incident occurs; logs cannot be filtered by tenant or stitched into a single request, and the apply path emitted no log at all, so root-cause analysis has almost no signal.
findings.short_summary: Plaintext logs, no ids, ~5 log sites in engine

findings.title: /markting/info is unauthenticated and discloses approver identities and account aliases
findings.description: The /markting/info handler has no bearer caller dependency (unlike sibling routes) yet returns approvers (sorted approval_policy.approver_refs), account aliases, write_provider, kill_switch, writes_enabled, and mode to any unauthenticated caller.
findings.recommendation: Require the bearer caller dependency on /markting/info or strip approvers/aliases from the unauthenticated response; keep liveness endpoints free of tenant data.
findings.failure_scenario: An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the engine host GETs /markting/info and enumerates approver user identifiers, account aliases, and the live write-safety posture for targeting/timing.
findings.short_summary: Unauth /markting/info leaks approvers and aliases

findings.title: Cloud log redaction is narrower than the engine's and can leak credential-shaped values
findings.description: reads.ts redacts only bearer/token/secret/authorization followed by a delimiter, then slices to 500 chars; http.ts logs the raw Error with no redaction. The engine's redaction covers Slack xox*/xapp-, sk-/sk-ant-, Google AIza, pb_, generic key:value, and postgres:// URLs. A provider error embedding an AIza/sk-/pb_/postgres DSN would be logged unredacted in the cloud.
findings.recommendation: Reuse a shared redaction routine mirroring the engine patterns across all cloud log/error paths, including http.ts before console.error(error).
findings.failure_scenario: A provider returns an error string containing an API key (e.g. AIza... or a postgres:// DSN); reads.ts/http.ts write it verbatim to cloud stdout and log aggregation.
findings.short_summary: Cloud redaction misses many secret shapes

findings.title: Cloud logging is inconsistent and carries no tenant/trace context
findings.description: Of 9 console sites, some emit structured JSON and some emit free-form strings/raw objects; none include organizationId/userId/request id even where the principal is in scope (reads.ts has principal.organizationId). There is no middleware.ts and no request-level access log.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one structured logger, always attach org/user/request ids, and add a request-level access log via middleware.
findings.failure_scenario: During triage, logs cannot be filtered by tenant or correlated into a request, and mixed JSON/plaintext formats break structured ingestion.
findings.short_summary: Mixed log formats, no tenant/trace context

findings.title: LangSmith tracing is documented but not actually enabled, and the cloud write path is untraced
findings.description: Docs/env claim LANGSMITH_API_KEY 'serves tracing', but no LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2/LANGSMITH_TRACING flag is set or documented (grep => 0), so the key alone (used for the gateway, sandboxes, mda deploy) does not by itself produce traces. Even if enabled, LangSmith only traces the engine's LangGraph runs; the adport/cloud apply path has no tracing.
findings.recommendation: Either wire and document the tracing flag explicitly or correct the docs; add a shared trace id propagated cloud -> engine so the apply path is observable regardless of LangSmith.
findings.failure_scenario: Operators set LANGSMITH_API_KEY expecting traces per the docs, but no traces appear; and the write-critical cloud bridge/apply is never traced either way.
findings.short_summary: Docs imply tracing the key does not enable

Did not exhaustively trace the adport core PolicyEngine/registry internals to confirm applyPending writes no internal audit outside cloud audit_events (verified only the cloud route and bridge). Did not deeply audit infra/ manifests for a possible deployment-level log/metrics sidecar.

Read-only audit; no writes, no credentials, no git changes.

findings.title: No graceful shutdown or connection draining; deploys can hang or drop in-flight work
findings.description: uvicorn is run with only host/port/log_level and no timeout_graceful_shutdown; there is no FastAPI lifespan. The sync Postgres pool (postgres.py close() defined but never called) and the async checkpointer pool (self_hosted.py:52-59 opened, never closed) are never drained on SIGTERM. Routes allow runs up to 300s, so shutdown either stalls on an in-flight request or is SIGKILLed.
findings.recommendation: Add a FastAPI lifespan that closes the repository and checkpointer pools; set a bounded timeout_graceful_shutdown; align orchestrator grace period; drain the report lock before exit.

findings.title: Report index is a single global, file-based, 50-entry store shared across all tenants
findings.description: All organizations' report runs are written to one JSON file (markting-reports.json) in the workspace volume, capped at 50 entries globally (entries[:50]); reports_list returns the whole index and the adport route forwards it with no organizationId filter. Writes are guarded only by an in-process asyncio.Lock and the file is unaffected by DATABASE_URL, so it is not durable in the DB nor safe across replicas.
findings.recommendation: Move the report index into Postgres keyed by organization, scope the adport route by organizationId, replace the global cap with per-tenant retention, and remove the local-file + in-process-lock design. (Defer the cross-tenant P0 security classification to the security/multi-tenancy workstream.)

findings.title: Kill switch is a per-process local file; it does not propagate across replicas
findings.description: kill_switch_engaged() is a local filesystem exists() check on workspace/KILL_SWITCH. In a multi-replica live self-hosted deployment with per-replica volumes, engaging it on one node does not stop writes on others, and if the workspace volume is not persisted across redeploys a previously-engaged switch is silently cleared. Latent in the shipped proposal-only host but inherited by the live write path.
findings.recommendation: Back the kill switch with shared state (DB row/shared config) checked on every write; ensure any file fallback lives on cluster-shared persistent storage; require engagement to reach all replicas.

findings.title: Health endpoint is shallow: never probes Postgres or the model (false-healthy)
findings.description: /health returns static runtime metadata with no DB ping or model reachability check, yet the compose healthcheck and cloud.depends_on.condition:service_healthy treat it as readiness. With Postgres down the node stays 'healthy' and the cloud keeps routing traffic that then fails.
findings.recommendation: Split liveness (/health) from readiness (/ready that runs SELECT 1 and reports pool saturation); point healthcheck and depends_on at readiness.

findings.title: Single process / single event loop with synchronous Postgres repos on the loop
findings.description: The engine is one asyncio process; proposal/approval/receipt repos use a blocking psycopg ConnectionPool (max_size=4) whose save/get calls run directly inside async handlers (not via to_thread), blocking the event loop per DB round-trip and serialising concurrent requests. No limit_concurrency and no horizontal-scaling story that keeps shared state consistent.
findings.recommendation: Offload sync repo calls with asyncio.to_thread (pattern already used in tools/reads.py:209, middleware/offload.py:61) or adopt async repos; size the pool for target concurrency; define an externalised-state scale-out plan.

findings.title: No server-side request timeout; client abort does not cancel the run; report lock held for whole run
findings.description: The timeout chain is client-side only (model 120s < client 240s < route 300s). The engine has no per-request timeout; a client fetch abort does not cancel the server coroutine, and the process-wide asyncio.Lock around /reports/run is held for the entire run, so a stuck/slow report blocks all other report runs (head-of-line blocking).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the engine handler in asyncio.wait_for with a server budget below the client timeout; make the report lock finer-grained or use DB concurrency; honour client disconnects.

findings.title: No resource limits, restart backoff caps, grace periods, or healthcheck start_period
findings.description: Neither compose file sets memory/CPU limits, stop_grace_period, replica config, or healthcheck start_period; services use restart: unless-stopped only. A runaway report render can OOM the host with no guardrail, crash-loop is uncapped, and early-boot failures count against the retry budget.
findings.recommendation: Set memory/CPU limits and reservations, add stop_grace_period aligned with the graceful-shutdown bound, add healthcheck start_period, and cap restart behaviour.

findings.title: No metrics, readiness, or tracing surface
findings.description: grep for prometheus/metrics/ready/livez/opentelemetry returns nothing across engine, demo host, and markting cloud libs; the only observability is logging.basicConfig INFO to stderr. The proposed SLOs cannot be measured with what ships.
findings.recommendation: Add a Prometheus /metrics endpoint (latency/count/in-flight, pool saturation), structured JSON logs with request IDs, and optional OTel traces around model and DB calls.

findings.title: Schema bootstrap runs on every boot with no versioning or migration lock
findings.description: Every instance runs CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plus AsyncPostgresSaver.setup() at boot. Concurrent boots can race on index creation / checkpointer migrations; there is no schema version table or advisory lock, and rollback across a langgraph checkpointer schema version is unguarded.
findings.recommendation: Gate setup() behind a Postgres advisory lock; introduce an explicit versioned migration run once per deploy; pin and test checkpointer schema across rollback versions.

findings.title: In-memory fallback (no DATABASE_URL) loses pending interrupts, dedupe, and thread ownership on restart
findings.description: When DATABASE_URL is unset the engine uses InMemoryDedupeStore/InMemoryThreadOwnershipStore and InMemorySaver (per-process). A restart drops pending interrupts/dedupe/thread ownership and a second replica cannot see another's threads; OPERATIONS.md acknowledges 'A restart loses pending proposals'. The shipped compose sets DATABASE_URL, but even in Postgres mode the report index stays file-based (H4-02), so Postgres mode is not fully stateless-restartable.
findings.recommendation: Make DATABASE_URL mandatory for any hosted deploy (fail boot if unset outside explicit local-demo); move the report index to Postgres so Postgres mode is genuinely restart-safe and scalable.

key_findings: No graceful shutdown: uvicorn runs with defaults, no FastAPI lifespan, and the Postgres/checkpointer pools are never closed — rolling deploys either hang on a 300s in-flight request or get SIGKILLed (serve_demo.py:411, postgres.py:64).

The report index is one global 50-entry JSON file in the workspace volume, returned to all callers with no org filter and guarded only by an in-process lock — not durable in the DB, not tenant-partitioned, and unsafe to scale horizontally (serve_demo.py:62,304,355; reports/engine/route.ts:16).
The kill switch (the core write-safety control) is a per-process local-file check, so it does not propagate across replicas and can be lost on a fresh volume (writes.py:195).
/health is liveness-only — it never probes Postgres or the model — yet compose depends_on treats it as readiness, so DB outages are invisible (api/app.py:80).

Single event loop with synchronous psycopg repo calls (max_size=4) invoked inside async handlers blocks the loop and serialises concurrency; no server-side request timeout and no observability (/metrics, tracing) exist.
No resource limits, stop_grace_period, or healthcheck start_period in either compose file; schema DDL runs unversioned on every boot with no advisory lock.

In-memory fallback (no DATABASE_URL) is strictly single-instance and loses pending interrupts/dedupe/thread ownership on restart; even Postgres mode is not fully stateless because the report index stays on disk.
H4.disagreements: OPERATIONS.md says compose 'persists checkpoints and local artifacts' — true for checkpoints/pgdata/workspace volumes, but it understates that the report index is only a local file (serve_demo.py:62,246-307), so Postgres mode is neither fully durable nor horizontally scalable. docker-compose.yml treats engine /health as readiness via depends_on.condition:service_healthy, but /health (api/app.py:80-89) is liveness-only with no DB/model probe. README's 'not production-ready' section honestly notes the single service token and that tenant isolation lives in adport tables, not the engine, but it does not disclose that the report index is a single global file visible across tenants (H4-02). OPERATIONS.md's 'a restart loses pending proposals; the code fails closed' is confirmed for the in-memory profile and not contradicted.
