H5.scope: DB operations across the two Postgres instances: Supabase (adport + markting_* bridge) migration/retention/indexes/pooling and the engine's self-hosted Postgres (pma_* repos + LangGraph checkpointer) bootstrap, pooling, and growth. Files: platform/supabase/migrations/*.sql, platform/supabase/config.toml, platform/apps/cloud/lib/db.ts, platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/repository.ts, platform/apps/cloud/next.config.ts, infra/cloud.Dockerfile, engine persistence/postgres.py, runtime/self_hosted.py, services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py, Makefile, docker-compose files, docs, and the DB integration test.

findings.title: markting_* bridge tables excluded from retention job (unbounded JSONB growth)
findings.description: The newest migration adds markting_engine_proposals (one upsert row per proposal+revision, full proposal+translation JSONB), markting_threads, markting_sandbox_state, markting_account_aliases, but never extends private.apply_data_retention(). Only an org cascade delete ever removes them.
findings.recommendation: Add these tables to apply_data_retention() keyed on organization_settings.data_retention_days (engine proposals by created_at, threads by last_message_at), add a covering index, and test the pruning.

findings.title: Engine Postgres instance has no retention/pruning of any kind
findings.description: engine-db stores LangGraph checkpoints (full graph/message state, never pruned) plus pma_proposals/receipts/approvals/dedupe/thread_owners; pma_dedupe adds one permanent row per event. No cron or cleanup exists under engine/. The demo host persists here when DATABASE_URL is set.
findings.recommendation: Implement and document engine-side retention (delete old checkpoints by updated_at, old pma_dedupe rows) or a cron; state explicitly that engine-db has no automatic retention.

findings.title: No production migration runbook; only documented apply path is destructive supabase db reset
findings.description: The entire documented/scripted apply path is `supabase db reset --local --yes`, which drops and recreates the DB. Production is referenced only as 'the normal migration process' with no command, ordering, pg_cron enablement, or rollback. Several migrations run cron.schedule/create extension assuming managed Supabase.
findings.recommendation: Add a production DB migration runbook (supabase db push ordering, pre-migration backup, pg_cron enablement, rollback) and warn that db reset is local-only.

findings.title: Cloud pool max:10 with a direct (non-pooler) URL is unsafe on the supported serverless target
findings.description: db() uses postgres({max:10, prepare:false}); prepare:false implies pgbouncer intent, but the sample SUPABASE_DB_URL points at the direct Postgres port 55322, not the transaction pooler. next.config sets output undefined when VERCEL, so serverless is a supported target where max:10 per warm instance multiplies into connection exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: For serverless require the Supabase transaction pooler URL and a low max (1-3); document per-target pool math; keep the direct URL only for the standalone container.

findings.title: Idempotent DDL at every engine boot: multi-replica race and no schema-evolution path
findings.description: setup() runs the full CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS block (and LangGraph saver.setup()) on every process start. CREATE IF NOT EXISTS is not fully concurrency-safe (can deadlock under simultaneous replica startup) and can never ALTER an existing pma_* table, so there is no engine schema-evolution path.
findings.recommendation: Gate setup() behind an advisory lock or one-shot init job; add a real migration tool for the engine schema.

findings.title: Two connection pools per engine process (up to 8 connections) undocumented
findings.description: Each engine process opens a sync repos pool (1-4) AND a separate async checkpointer pool (1-4) against engine-db, up to 8 connections per process, more than the per-pool 4 the comments imply. No runbook states the aggregate vs engine-db max_connections across replicas.
findings.recommendation: Document combined pool sizing (8 x replicas) and provision engine-db max_connections / a pooler accordingly.

findings.title: No statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on either client or role
findings.description: Neither the adport_backend role, the paid_media engine user, nor the clients set statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout; only a single local lock_timeout exists in one migration. A hung query or abandoned transaction can pin a pooled connection indefinitely.

findings.title: Nightly retention delete on pending_operations uses an unindexed expression

findings.title: Master encryption key has no KMS/escrow; a DB restore is useless without it
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/crypto.ts:5-9 single 32-byte key from env ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY

findings.description: Credential confidentiality rests on one symmetric key in an env var/.env with no KMS, escrow, or separate backup. A DB backup alone is non-restorable without the matching key (all ciphertext undecryptable); a backup bundling the key leaks all tenant credentials. No documented procedure resolves this tension.
findings.recommendation: Move the key to a KMS/secret manager with its own backup and access policy; document that restore requires recovering the correct key version separately from the DB.

findings.title: Key rotation documented and schema-provisioned but not implemented; rotation would destroy all ciphertext

rg key_version platform --type ts finds no code reading it to select a key; no re-encrypt tool exists
findings.description: The key_version column exists but no multi-key decryption path or bulk re-encrypt job exists. Rotating ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY in place makes every stored ciphertext fail its GCM auth tag — a self-inflicted data-loss event. Documented rotation is not achievable with current code.
findings.recommendation: Implement envelope rotation: a keyring keyed by key_version, write at current version, and a re-encrypt job that rewrites old versions to the new one.

findings.description: Every Assistant turn and report run invokes the LLM engine (the main variable cost), but the only guard is a flat plan-independent 120 req/min rate limit. No usage_events table, no per-org AI/report quotas, no token/cost accounting, no Stripe metered price. Plans gate only accounts/members/retention/write. findings.title: Churned (fully canceled) customers are locked out of re-subscribing in-app
findings.description: startSubscription refuses whenever entitlement.providerSubscriptionId is set. On customer.subscription.deleted, applySubscription keeps provider_subscription_id and getOrganizationEntitlement returns it regardless of status. The Stripe portal cannot resurrect a deleted subscription, so a fully-churned org has no self-serve path back to a paid plan.
findings.recommendation: Gate startSubscription on an active-ish status (active/trialing/past_due/unpaid) rather than mere presence of providerSubscriptionId, or clear provider_subscription_id on subscription.deleted while retaining provider_customer_id.

findings.title: Webhook idempotency guard is not atomic with the effect it protects
findings.description: processStripeEvent reads private.billing_events for dedup, calls applySubscription (its own transaction), then inserts the event id in a separate statement afterward. Concurrent redeliveries both pass the select and both apply; a crash between the applySubscription commit and the billing_events insert causes reprocessing.
findings.recommendation: Insert the billing_events row inside the same transaction as applySubscription before applying the effect, using the event_id PK + on conflict do nothing to short-circuit duplicates atomically.

findings.title: Webhook applies events without ordering/recency guards; out-of-order Stripe delivery can regress state
findings.description: applySubscription unconditionally overwrites plan/status/period from whatever event arrives, with no comparison to stored state or event created timestamp. Stripe does not guarantee ordering, so a stale subscription.updated after a newer event overwrites with older data.
findings.recommendation: Guard the update with a monotonic marker (store Stripe created/last_event_at and only apply newer events) or re-fetch the authoritative subscription from Stripe inside the handler.

findings.title: Free reader and past_due both retain full engine access; no payment-failure downgrade path
findings.description: past_due keeps the paid plan and there is no invoice.payment_failed handler; downgrade relies solely on Stripe eventually sending unpaid/canceled. Combined with I3-01, delinquent and Free orgs both consume unmetered paid engine capacity.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit dunning policy (restrict after N days past_due) and combine with metering (I3-01) so the cost ceiling holds regardless of billing status.

findings.title: Demo seed grants a paid plan by direct DB write with no environment guard
findings.description: seed-demo.mjs bypasses Stripe and sets plan='operator', status='active' directly, with no NODE_ENV/localhost guard; it uses whatever SUPABASE_DB_URL/.env is supplied. Seeded orgs have no provider_subscription_id so webhooks never reconcile them. Legitimate dev convenience but reachable against prod if misconfigured.
findings.recommendation: Guard the seed to refuse non-local DB URLs unless an explicit opt-in flag is set, and document that seeded orgs are unbilled.

findings.title: applySubscription trusts subscription.metadata.organizationId without binding it to the customer
findings.description: When metadata.organizationId is present it is used directly as the target org, skipping the customer/subscription lookup, without verifying the event customer id matches the org's stored provider_customer_id. Low risk since metadata is first-party and events are signature-verified, but the missing cross-check removes defense-in-depth and unique columns can cause webhook failures on mismatch.
findings.recommendation: After resolving via metadata, assert the resolved org's stored provider_customer_id is null or equals the event customer id before overwriting.

findings.title: Webhook applySubscription path lacks runnable unit coverage (status mapping, downscaling boundaries)
findings.description: Only a DB-backed integration test covers processStripeEvent (one subscription.deleted downscaling case) and it needs a live Supabase DB. subscriptionStatus mapping over all statuses, getOrganizationEntitlement downgrade thresholds, and the slice(maxActiveAccounts) off-by-one have no fast unit tests.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for subscriptionStatus over every Stripe status, getOrganizationEntitlement downgrade boundaries, and the downscaling slice including off-by-one cases.

key_findings: No usage metering exists for AI turns, report runs, or tokens — the product's dominant variable cost is unbilled and uncapped per plan; only a flat 120 req/min rate limit guards it (P1).
Plans gate only static resources (accounts/members/retention/write); members, accounts, and retention limits ARE enforced; clientWorkspaces flag is defined but never enforced.
Churned (fully canceled) orgs cannot re-subscribe in-app because provider_subscription_id persists and startSubscription blocks on its presence (P2).

Webhook idempotency is non-atomic (dedup insert happens after the effect, outside the transaction) and there are no event ordering/recency guards, allowing double-processing and state regression (P2).

Stripe integration is otherwise solid: Checkout with 7-day trial + owner-only guard (test-passing), billing portal, signature verification, and correct modern-API item.current_period_end mapping for SDK v22.5.0.
past_due retains full paid entitlement and there is no invoice.payment_failed dunning handler (P2).
Demo seed (seed-demo.mjs:44) grants a paid plan via direct DB write with no environment guard — a prod foot-gun, not runtime code (P3).

findings.title: Non-atomic pending-operation consume lets a concurrent or retried apply execute the provider write twice
findings.short_summary: Double-apply race executes provider write twice
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:413-418 (delete is unconditional `update set consumed_at=now()`, no `consumed_at is null` guard, no returning/rowcount)
F9 cmd8: node f9-double-apply.mjs => applyWriteCalls: 2, audit [validated,applied,applied]
F6 cmd1 and F7 harness E2/E3/E4 reproduce the same
findings.failure_scenario: Two admins click Apply on the same pending id (or one client retries after a timeout, or an MCP client resends tools/call) within the provider round-trip window; both pass pending.get, both call provider.applyWrite, both append 'applied'. For a create tool this is a duplicate budgeted campaign; a post-write failure before delete also leaves the row applicable for a later replay.
findings.description: The adport PolicyEngine and the Postgres PendingOperationStore never claim the pending row before the provider call. The 'exactly one approved execution per preview' invariant the whole two-step design rests on is not enforced under concurrency. Reproduced at runtime against the file-backed store; the Postgres store has identical SQL shape (VERIFIED_CODE). Mitigated to P1 (not P0) because default policy coerces created campaigns to PAUSED and the two bridge-mapped tools write absolute values.
findings.recommendation: Claim before writing: `update pending_operations set consumed_at=now() where id=$1 and organization_id=$2 and consumed_at is null and expires_at>now() returning *`; treat zero rows as PENDING_NOT_FOUND and only the winner calls applyWrite. Record the provider result in the same statement/outbox; pass an idempotency key to providers that support one. Add a concurrent-apply test and an apply-vs-reject test (F6/F7/F8 C2-C4).

findings.title: Apply/reject are multi-statement without a transaction: reject cannot stop an in-flight apply, an executed write can leave no audit event, and a provider failure leaves the row applicable
findings.short_summary: Non-transactional apply/reject; silent audit gaps
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/approvals/[id]/reject/route.ts:16-21 (delete -> recordAudit -> markPendingOutcome, three statements, no db().begin)
platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:113-123 (applyWrite -> audit.append -> delete, no try/catch around applyWrite)
F7 harness E2: audit 'applied' append fails after applyWrite => audit shows only [validated], row stays open, retry => applyWrite 2
findings.failure_scenario: Approver A applies while approver B rejects: A passes get() before B's delete, then writes anyway -> audit shows rejected then applied. Or Postgres fails between statements: a consumed row with no rejected audit, or an applied operation whose provenance stays pending, or (F8-11) a provider accepts the mutation but audit.append throws so the ad change happened with no 'applied' record.
findings.description: A human reject is not authoritative once an apply has started, and the audit trail - the product's accountability story - can be silent about a real ad-platform mutation. F6-02, F7-02, F7-07, F8-11 consolidated.
findings.recommendation: Put consume + audit + provenance update in one db().begin; derive provenance from the pending row instead of storing it twice; wrap applyWrite in try/catch that writes an apply_failed marker and decides explicitly whether a failed pending id remains usable; make a reject that wins the claim fail the apply.

findings.recommendation: Before registry.call, look up findEngineProposal(org, proposal_id, revision) and reuse the open pending row; only bridge when outcome.interrupted is true or dedupe by payload digest; add an engine-side sweep that rejects proposals older than N minutes.

findings.title: Engine error translation leaks 4xx detail to the browser, relays engine 401 as a user 401, and the friendly 5xx messages are dead code; infra errors are reported as policy rejections
findings.short_summary: Error-translation leak and dead-code 5xx messages
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/engine-client.ts:101-107 (message embeds up to 300 chars of upstream body)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/http.ts:26-28 (any status >=500 rewritten to 'Internal server error.', so assistant.ts:45 'not reachable' message is unreachable)
F4 harness: reports GET engine 401 => 401 with engine detail text; assistant engine 403 => 403 with raw body

platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/bridge.ts:76-83 (any thrown error at preview -> code 'ERROR', status rejected_by_policy, engine told 'adport refused the preview'); F7 scratch F3 confirms a pg connection error is indistinguishable from POLICY_VIOLATION
findings.failure_scenario: A misconfigured MARKTING_ENGINE_TOKEN surfaces to end users as HTTP 401 with the engine's detail text; a Postgres error inside validate is recorded in provenance and told to the engine thread as a policy refusal, and the user gets a generic 500 because the curated 503 message is discarded.
findings.description: Operational confusion plus minor information disclosure (engine internals, bearer-token wording). F4-04, F7-03, F7-06 consolidated.
findings.recommendation: Map engine errors to a fixed vocabulary (502/503 with stable codes engine_unavailable/engine_misconfigured), never relay engine 401/403 as user auth statuses, let apiError keep curated 5xx messages, and branch bridge errors on AdportError{POLICY_VIOLATION,INVALID_INPUT,PROVIDER_ERROR} vs unknown (record status 'error', return 503, do not tell the engine 'refused').

findings.title: Engine report runs are not plan-gated and effectively unlimited; one member can monopolise the single engine lock; invalid dates are forwarded
findings.short_summary: Unmetered report runs can DoS the shared engine
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/reports/engine/route.ts:31-35 (only viewer refused; no requireScope, no plan check; per-org limit 120/min)
services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:324,344 (every run serialises on one process-wide asyncio.Lock, each renders HTML/PDF)
F4 harness: reports POST member reader-plan => 200; cadence=yearly end=2026-13-99 => 200 (invalid date passes the regex and is forwarded)
docs/TODO.md:8 admits engine usage is not metered
findings.failure_scenario: Any member of any free org queues up to 120 renders/min on the single engine process, blocking other tenants' report runs and assistant turns that share the lock.
findings.description: Report runs are not entitlement-gated and the engine is a shared serialised resource. F4-06.
findings.recommendation: Gate POST /api/reports/engine on a plan entitlement, lower the per-org limit (a few per hour), validate end as a real date, and return 429/409 when the engine lock is busy.

findings.title: Requesting an org you are not a member of returns 500 instead of 403
findings.short_summary: Non-member org probe yields 500, not 403
evidence: routes translate only 'Authentication required.' (apply/route.ts:30, reject/route.ts:24, reports/engine/route.ts:10, assistant/messages/route.ts:17); lib/http.ts:21,26-29 maps any other Error to 500 + console.error
F4 harness: apply/reject/reports wrong org => 500 each
findings.failure_scenario: A trivial probe with another tenant's organizationId produces server-error noise and a misleading 'something broke' message rather than a clean 403; no data is leaked (the membership check holds).
findings.description: Downgraded from F4's P2 to P3: no data exposure, UX/alerting hygiene only. F4-03.
findings.recommendation: Throw HttpError(...,403) from resolveMembership or translate that message alongside the authentication one in a shared helper.

findings.title: Stripe webhook dedupe is check-then-act with no ordering guard
findings.short_summary: Non-atomic webhook dedupe; out-of-order events overwrite newer state
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/billing.ts:120-123 (select by event_id), :126-131 (applySubscription), :132-136 (insert on conflict do nothing AFTER processing)
supabase/migrations/20260828120000_cloud_plans_and_account_scope.sql:51-55 (event_id is PK, so insert-first would work)
billing.ts:77-87 (plan/status applied last-writer-wins, no event.created comparison)
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent deliveries of one event both pass the pre-check and both run applySubscription (duplicate audit rows); a stale customer.subscription.updated arriving after a newer one over Stripe's multi-day retry window overwrites the newer plan/entitlement and disables ad accounts under the wrong cap.
findings.description: Idempotent for the same event sequentially, but not under concurrency and not ordered. F6-04, F7-09 consolidated.
findings.recommendation: Insert the marker first (insert on conflict do nothing returning; zero rows => duplicate) inside the same transaction as applySubscription, and ignore events whose created is older than the stored subscription's last applied timestamp; return 500 (not 400) for processing errors.

findings.title: Budget policy is not re-evaluated at apply time (validate->apply TOCTOU)
findings.short_summary: Percentage budget rail not re-checked at apply
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:110-111 (re-runs only checkStaticPolicy; comment says 'Policy may have changed... re-check')
engine.ts:62 (checkBudgetPolicy runs only in validate, against preview.budgetDeltas.fromMicros captured at validate time)
sandbox-provider.ts:144-147 (CAS compares state loaded inside applyWrite, not preview-time state); real providers have no CAS
findings.failure_scenario: Within pending_ttl_minutes a concurrent op lowers the live budget; apply still writes the validate-time value, exceeding the percentage cap relative to the new baseline (e.g. validate 12.4M->15.4M at 24% while another op drops to 10M; apply writes 15.4M, a 54% jump).
findings.description: The percentage-delta rail can be exceeded under concurrent edits or a tightened policy. Absolute cap is unaffected (depends only on toMicros). F6-03, F8-06 consolidated.
findings.recommendation: In apply, re-run previewWrite + checkBudgetPolicy (or store a policy hash in the pending row and refuse on mismatch), or fail with PENDING_MISMATCH when the live baseline differs from preview.budgetDeltas[].fromMicros.

findings.title: No test ever runs cloud code against the engine host; the wire contract is held only by hand-written fixtures and unvalidated casts
findings.short_summary: No cloud<->engine contract test; EngineOutcome cast unvalidated

services/engine-demo/tests/test_demo_api.py exercises the engine API only; no test drives EngineClient against a booted host
findings.failure_scenario: An upstream engine sync renames a field (e.g. available_actions) or changes the platform enum/unit; the Assistant breaks at runtime while unit tests on both sides stay green.
findings.description: text, interrupted, available_actions, receipt and the report-run shape flow to the UI unvalidated. The compose stack is the only place both sides meet and was verified only manually. F2-06, F8 scenario H8.

findings.title: No committed e2e/browser suite; the phase reports' Playwright walkthroughs are unreproducible

findings.title: Six providers silently cap report rows without setting truncated; Meta/TikTok/Apple pagination is untested or missing
findings.short_summary: Silent report truncation under-counts spend on large accounts
evidence: meta/src/provider.ts:181-192, google/src/provider.ts:177-182, tiktok/src/provider.ts:129-132, apple/src/provider.ts:175 return a prefix with no truncated flag; grep -c truncated = 0 in apple/google/meta/microsoft/reddit/tiktok src
tiktok/src/provider.ts:112,196-197 and apple/src/provider.ts:125,175 fetch only page 1; no multi-page fixture in tiktok.test.ts/apple.test.ts
contrast: linkedin/pinterest/snapchat/spotify/x set and test truncated and loop pages
findings.failure_scenario: An AI media buyer summing spend/conversions across report rows on an account with more entities than one page/limit receives a silent prefix indistinguishable from a complete report, under-counts, and may conclude budgets are under-delivering - feeding wrong recommendations into the audit/apply chain.
findings.description: Upstream adport code, but directly material to the media-buyer product. The six older providers test the happy wire shape but not the limit/pagination paths the five newer ones cover routinely. F5-03, F5-04 (and the uneven-depth F5-05) consolidated.
findings.recommendation: Set truncated=true whenever the slice/page cap is hit; loop pagination for TikTok (page_info.total_page) and Apple (offset/totalCount) bounded by limit; add a two-page fixture and a limit test per provider mirroring the LinkedIn one.

findings.title: Apply/reject look the pending row up in a 200-row window; older valid rows return a misleading 404

platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts:420-425 (sweep sets consumed_at), :397 (get filters consumed_at is null), :700 (dashboard filters expires_at>now())

findings.description: Error-code fidelity only. F8-09.

findings.title: DB-gated suites gate on env presence not DB reachability; a stale .env.local turns skips into failures

findings.title: Body handling on session routes: malformed JSON silently accepted, null body 500s, no size cap or CSRF/content-type check
findings.short_summary: Weak request-body hygiene on mutating routes
evidence: request.json().catch(()=>({})) at apply/route.ts:16, reject/route.ts:10, reports/engine/route.ts:29, assistant/messages/route.ts:11

findings.title: Engine-side reject edge cases: duplicate reject is an unhandled 500 and a late reject resumes the wrong interrupt
findings.short_summary: Duplicate reject 500; late reject hits the current interrupt

findings.title: The translator ignores after[].unit (contradicting ARCHITECTURE.md) and no currency assertion exists anywhere in the chain
findings.short_summary: unit ignored; currency never checked

translate.ts:52-53 (currency 'used for the human preview only', never read); SANDBOX_ACCOUNTS mixes USD and SAR (sandbox-provider.ts:43-47)

findings.description: Correct today by coincidence (engine emits exactly one unit). F8-07, F8-08.
findings.recommendation: Treat unit as part of the contract (accept only 'account currency per day' or null, else unsupported); bind alias currency to the provider account's reported currency at preview and flag a mismatch as unsupported.

key_findings: P1 (reproduced at runtime by F6 and independently by F9): the two-step apply is not atomic - two concurrent/retried applies of one pending id both call provider.applyWrite (applyWriteCalls: 2). The 'single-use pending id' invariant the whole safety design rests on is only true sequentially.
The only human-approval surface (apply/reject/assistant/reports routes and their scope/role/self-approval/tenant gates) has ZERO automated tests at any layer; make test and CI never touch it.

There is no CI at the monorepo root; the nested vendored workflows never run for this repo, and make test exercises ~63 of 500+ cases, omitting the PolicyEngine, every DB-gated suite, the 177-test engine suite, and all build/typecheck/lint.

Running the engine host once writes engine/workspace/KILL_SWITCH into the vendored tree, turning 19 safety-critical upstream engine tests red (reproduced: 19 failed/158 passed/3 skipped); make test never runs that suite so the poisoning is invisible.

Engine reports are not tenant-scoped (any org reads any report) and four-eyes approval is disabled by default in .env.example and bypassable via REST/MCP - both latent data/authorization risks that are only masked today by forced synthetic data and single-user demos.

Green tests are not readiness: the strong green layer covers what the bridge does with a proposal, not who may apply it, concurrency, tenant isolation, the engine wire contract, or any browser flow; the phase-report Playwright walkthroughs have no committed artifact and are unreproducible.

Every F1-F8 specialist's load-bearing evidence held under F9 spot-check; where severities differed the highest defensible one was taken with the conditional recorded (e.g. cross-tenant reports P2 today / P0 with real data).
F9.disagreements: Docs vs code contradictions confirmed across the team and re-verified by F9: policy-engine.test.ts:100 'Pending id is single-use' holds only sequentially (two concurrent applies both succeed); UPSTREAM.md 'no engine file modified' is true only for tracked files (the host writes a gitignored KILL_SWITCH that breaks 19 upstream tests); PHASE0-REPORT.md:51 '177 passed' is not reproducible in this checkout (19 fail until the kill-switch path is redirected); the PHASE1/2 Playwright walkthroughs have no committed script and cannot be reproduced; .env.example:49 ships MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true while the README calls it 'single-user demos only' and the schema default is false; ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 says the bridge must use each after[].unit but translate.ts:148-151 never reads it; ARCHITECTURE.md:367 calls private.billing_events 'idempotency' but the marker is written after processing with a non-atomic pre-check (sequential dedupe only). No F-agent finding failed an F9 spot-check; the only calibration change was keeping cross-tenant reports at P2 today (P0 with real data) because serve_demo forces DATA_MODE=sample, and treating the zero-route-test gap as a GAP (security-relevant) rather than a defect.
F9.not_verified: The Postgres double-apply at the SQL layer (no DB in sandbox; VERIFIED_CODE only - identical delete shape to the file store, which F9 did reproduce). The DB-gated and HTTP-gated suites' live pass/fail (ECONNREFUSED 55322; assertions read, not executed). pnpm build / build:standalone at HEAD and both Docker images (sandbox network blocks builds; next-env.d.ts is tracked so build was not run). Live provider/Stripe/IdP behaviour and MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=live (no credentials, by design). LangGraph's response to a new message on an interrupted thread (S-E6, the trigger for the CC-08 replay). F9 did not re-run the provider package suites (F1 already did, all green); the F5 verdict rests on reading what those tests omit, not on re-execution. GitHub Actions ignoring nested .github is well-established platform behaviour, not exercised here (the absence of a root workflow is verified).

findings.title: AI surfaces analyse bundled fixtures, not the tenant's accounts, in both demo and live modes; UI calls it 'your connected accounts'
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/i18n/messages/assistant.ts:5 ('Ask about performance across your connected accounts')
grep paid_media_data_mode serve_demo.py => exit 0, :188 and :386 both 'sample'
findings.description: The engine powering the Assistant and the 'AI analysis reports' is pinned to the three bundled fixture accounts (demo-google/meta/reddit) in BOTH demo and live modes; MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=live only swaps the scripted replies for a real LLM, not the data. The tenant's OAuth-connected accounts are never passed to the engine, yet the UI/README present the output as analysis of the user's own accounts. This is the product's headline 'AI media buyer' promise and it is undeliverable today.
findings.recommendation: Either feed the engine the tenant's normalized report rows per turn via adport's scoped report/accounts_list tools (per-tenant credentials, org currency/goals/protected accounts in context), or relabel the Assistant and AI reports as 'demo' in both locales regardless of MARKTING_DEMO_MODE until a per-tenant data path exists. Do not let live-mode proposals reach a real account until the model's inputs are the tenant's data.

findings.title: Engine report list/files are global across tenants (unscoped listReports); P0 cross-tenant leak if engine carries real data
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/reports/engine/route.ts:18-20 (organizationId only validates session membership; listReports() called with no org filter)
platform/apps/cloud/app/api/reports/engine/[name]/route.ts (file download checks only that a session exists)
services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py (one markting-reports.json index for the whole engine, requested_by = shared token caller)
findings.description: The Reports page lists and downloads report runs from one engine instance shared by the entire deployment, with no per-organization filtering. Org A sees and can download Org B's runs. Today content is fixtures so no spend data leaks, but run history (timestamps, cadence) is shared and it becomes a cross-tenant disclosure the moment the engine is given real data.
findings.recommendation: Store run ids in a per-org table and filter listReports()/fetchReportFile() by the caller's organization; refuse downloads for runs the org does not own; add a test asserting an org cannot read another org's report run.

findings.title: Live-mode proposals require a hand-written SQL alias row; no alias-management UI
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/translate.ts (returns 'no adport account is mapped to engine alias' unless markting_account_aliases has a row)
infra/seed/seed-demo.mjs (demo seed inserts aliases via raw SQL)
findings.description: An operator who flips MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=false gets an Assistant that answers from fixtures and refuses every proposal with 'Proposal could not be mapped to an account' because no dashboard page, API route or onboarding step creates or shows engine aliases. The only AI->write path is therefore unusable in production without hand-written SQL.
findings.recommendation: Add an admin UI (Accounts page) binding an enabled organization_ad_accounts row to an engine alias with validation against the connected provider, and derive the engine account registry per organization rather than from a global TOML.

findings.title: 'Separate client workspaces' sold on live Stripe Agency/Enterprise checkout with zero implementation
evidence: grep -rn clientWorkspaces platform/apps/cloud => exit 0, only plans.ts def/values + billing/page.tsx:95
platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/billing/actions.ts (live Stripe checkout for the Agency plan)
findings.description: The clientWorkspaces entitlement flag is read only to render a billing bullet; no code creates, isolates or scopes a client workspace, and the data model is a flat single-tenant org. The Agency plan (EUR 149/mo) is purchasable via live Stripe checkout, so a paying agency is charged for a feature that does not exist - a representation/financial-risk exposure, not merely a missing feature. Reconciled to P1 (G6 rated P1; G1/I2 P2).
findings.recommendation: Either implement workspace partitioning (parent org + child workspaces with scoped connections, roles, reports, billing roll-up) or remove the flag, the bullet and the plan copy until it ships.

findings.title: No organization switcher; oldest-membership resolver strands invited members in their own empty org
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/components/shell.tsx (org name is static text, no switcher)
platform/supabase/migrations/20260817171039_cloud_initial_schema.sql (handle_new_user creates a personal org per signup)
findings.description: requireDashboardTenant always picks the user's oldest membership. A user invited to an agency/team workspace already has a personal org created at signup (always older), so they land in their own empty org and have no UI to switch to the org they were invited to. The sessionPrincipal/resolveMembership plumbing accepts an org id but no UI threads it.
findings.recommendation: Add an org switcher that threads a chosen org id through requestedOrganizationId, persist an active org, and route freshly-invited users to the inviting org on first login.

findings.title: One OAuth grant per provider per organization
findings.description: All of an org's accounts for a provider must be reachable from a single user token. Client accounts living in separate Business Managers with separate logins cannot be connected side by side, blocking agency/50-account onboarding.
findings.recommendation: Allow N connections per provider keyed by external grant id, or implement client workspaces each with its own connection set.

findings.title: Approval UX is undecidable: summary-only row, no reject reason, Apply shown to requester, 15-min TTL, no notifications
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/approvals/approval-actions.tsx (reject posts no reason though reject/route.ts accepts one; Apply shown by role only)
findings.description: The one person whose judgement the architecture depends on - the approver - sees the least information: a summary string and an id, on a 15-minute TTL, with no before/after, % delta, dry-run status, risk flags or engine reason, all of which are already loaded in the row. Reject offers no reason field though the API accepts one; Apply is rendered to the requester who will hit a 403; expiry is a bare UTC timestamp; no notification path exists.
findings.recommendation: Expand each row/drawer with changes, budgetDeltas (before->after, % delta, currency), coercions, serverValidated, engine before/after, risk+flags, full reason, measurement/reversal plans, requester identity and thread link, relative expiry; add a mandatory reject reason; hide Apply for the requester; notify approvers; make TTL plan/role aware or add re-validate.

findings.title: Overview KPIs sum spend across currencies and the blended ROAS tile is structurally 0x (conversion_value never requested)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/reads.ts:58 (summary from report tool is dropped)
findings.description: Two defects in the first screen a buyer sees: (1) totals reduce spend and conversion_value over all rows regardless of row.currency, so a SAR+AED+USD buyer gets a meaningless headline; (2) the blended ROAS tile is always 0x because conversion_value is never projected, while the per-row ROAS column shows real values - the page contradicts itself. The engine's per-currency spend-weighted summary is computed and then discarded.
findings.recommendation: Render summary.groups as one tile group per currency, request conversion_value (or use summary roas), and add a currency column to both tables.

findings.title: 'Findings' holds a primary nav slot but has no producer in the codebase - permanently empty
evidence: grep -rn '.save(|insert into public.findings' platform/apps/cloud => exit 0, no non-test caller of save
findings.description: Findings occupies one of eight primary nav slots and renders a severity/title/provider/account/status table, but no platform code path ever writes a finding row (both runtime builders only construct the store; the engine writes to its own store, not this cloud-Postgres table). In any normal deployment the page is permanently the empty state, indistinguishable from 'healthy'. Per the audit rule, code claiming a feature it does not deliver is a defect, not a gap.
findings.recommendation: Wire a producer (scheduled engine audit pass or a cloud job calling PostgresFindingsStore.save) or demote Findings out of primary nav until populated; document and verify the write path.

findings.title: No alerts / monitoring of any kind
evidence: no scheduler in docker-compose.yml / serve_demo.py / infra for engine reports or alerts
all 9 'alert' hits in the cloud app are role="alert" error callouts (e.g. provider-connections.tsx)
pg_cron jobs exist only for retention and selection expiry
findings.description: No budget-pacing, spend-anomaly, disapproved-ad, connection-error/token-expiry or pending-approval-reminder alerts, and no digest. Connection errors surface only when someone opens the Connections page. A 50-account media buyer has nothing watching the accounts between visits.
findings.recommendation: Add daily pacing vs budget, spend spikes/drops, CPA/ROAS drift vs targets, disapprovals, token/connection errors and pending-approval reminders, delivered by email/WhatsApp/Slack with per-account thresholds and a route to the affected entity.

findings.title: No bulk operations, saved views, filters, date ranges, drill-down or export on any data screen
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/accounts/account-access-manager.tsx:36-50 (one request + full refresh per row toggle)
findings.description: Windows are baked into routes; there is no date-range picker, period-over-period compare, entity drill-down (account->campaign->ad group->ad), sort/filter/search, saved views, bulk multi-select (except the OAuth picker), or CSV/Sheets/scheduled export anywhere. Enterprise and 50-account personas cannot operate at scale; the e-commerce persona cannot pivot by product/campaign type.
findings.recommendation: Add a date-range picker with compare, breakdowns and drill-down, sort/filter/search, saved views, multi-select bulk actions in one request, and CSV/Sheets export plus scheduled report delivery.

findings.title: Default Free/reader plan strips tools:write so previews/writes are impossible, while onboarding promises 'every write requires a preview'
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/tools/write.ts (the dry-run preview is the same readOnly:false tool, so previewing needs tools:write)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/i18n/messages/onboarding.ts:15 ('Every write requires an exact preview'); lib/cloud/auth.ts (raw 403 'API key lacks required scope: tools:write' on REST)
findings.description: Every new signup lands on Free/reader, which strips tools:write; because the preview is the first half of the same write tool, a Free user cannot even preview the thing onboarding presents as the core safety feature. Onboarding never discloses the plan, its limits, or that writes need Operator+. The MCP path degrades to a structured PLAN_LIMIT message, but the REST tool route and dashboard apply return the raw scope 403.
findings.recommendation: Add a plan/limits panel to onboarding stating Free is read-only and writes need Operator+, with an upgrade link; make the REST tool route and apply route return the same structured PLAN_LIMIT message the MCP path uses.

findings.title: Flat 4-role RBAC enforced ad hoc; no per-account/per-client/per-provider scoping; member access is org-wide
evidence: enforcement scattered: dashboard.ts:56-57, onboarding.ts:27, account-selection.ts:18, tenant-admin.ts:10-17, plans.ts:93, approvals/[id]/apply/route.ts:21
ad-account/findings RLS grants access to any member of the org (20260828120000_*.sql:102-115)
findings.description: Roles are a hard-coded enum enforced by ad hoc boolean checks per call site. There is no permission matrix, no custom/least-privilege roles, and no per-ad-account/per-provider/per-client access control: every invited member sees every account, finding and audit entry. Enterprises/agencies cannot express 'this user only touches Client X's Google account' or 'finance approves budgets only'.
findings.recommendation: Introduce resource-scoped permissions (per connection/ad-account), a declarative permission matrix, optional custom roles, and enforce per-account scoping in Postgres RLS and the bridge runtime.

findings.title: Assistant threads lost on reload; blocking composer, no streaming, raw <pre> rendering
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/assistant/assistant-chat.tsx (messages/threadId in useState only; textarea disabled while busy; replies in <pre>)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/repository.ts (listThreads + markting_threads exist but nothing in the UI calls listThreads)
findings.description: Assistant conversations live only in React state; the markting_threads table and listThreads exist but the UI never lists or replays threads, so a buyer cannot return to yesterday's analysis or find the thread that produced a pending operation. The composer blocks for minutes with no streaming, and replies render as raw <pre> with Markdown markers showing.
findings.recommendation: List and replay threads from markting_threads, link each pending operation to its thread, stream or poll, and render Markdown/tables.

findings.title: No enterprise identity: no SAML/OIDC SSO, no SCIM, MFA disabled in config - contradicts advertised 'Includes SSO'
evidence: no SCIM endpoint (find app -type d | grep scim => none)
findings.description: Authentication is Supabase email/password plus Google/GitHub consumer social OAuth. There is no SAML/enterprise OIDC IdP, no SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning, no domain auto-join, and the committed config disables TOTP and phone MFA with no org-level enforcement. This is a hard enterprise procurement blocker and contradicts the sold Enterprise 'Includes SSO' feature.
findings.recommendation: Add SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM provisioning gated behind the enterprise entitlement; enable TOTP/WebAuthn and add an org policy to require MFA with step-up on apply/delete.

findings.title: Audit trail non-compliant: capped/unfiltered UI, no export/SIEM, generic actor, hard-deleted by retention cron, actor nulled on delete, no IP/UA
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/audit/page.tsx (listAuditEvents(org,150), no export/filter/pagination; actor shown as generic member/api-key/system)
platform/supabase/migrations/20260817171039_cloud_initial_schema.sql:150-168 (actor_user_id on delete set null; no IP/user-agent columns)
findings.description: The audit view is a last-150-rows table with no export/SIEM, no time-range/actor/provider filters, and no per-actor attribution (actor_user_id is stored but never resolved to a name/email). Events are hard-deleted after data_retention_days with no archival, deleting a user nulls their audit attribution, and no source IP/user-agent is captured - the opposite of an immutable forensic trail, and the retention feature is sold as 'longer audit history' while it destroys history.
findings.recommendation: Add a paginated filterable audit view and a CSV/JSON export API plus SIEM streaming; resolve and display actor identity; capture IP/user-agent; snapshot actor email and restrict the FK action; archive to immutable/WORM storage before retention purge.

findings.title: No e-commerce commerce data (store revenue, catalog, feed, product-level, MER/CAC/LTV); proposals limited to budget/status
evidence: engine CREATIVE entity is read/normalized only (no creative analysis/fatigue surface)
findings.description: The e-commerce brand persona gets platform-attributed ROAS only - no store revenue, catalog, feed, or product-level view, and no MER/CAC/LTV/profit. Proposals are limited to budget and status changes; there is no creative, bidding, audience or feed action. Cross-references deliverable 09 (all e-commerce rows PARTIAL/MISSING).
findings.recommendation: Add e-commerce revenue connectors (Salla/Zid/Shopify) so ROAS uses store revenue, and broaden the proposal catalogue (bids, ad-set status, creative pausing, keyword negatives, audience exclusions) under the same guardrails.

findings.title: Timestamps are UTC with a hard-coded suffix and inconsistent formatting; approval expiry misreads by the Riyadh offset
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/assistant/assistant-chat.tsx and reports/engine-reports.tsx (bypass formatDate with toLocaleString, browser tz, different pattern => hydration mismatch)
approval expiry rendered via formatDate at approvals/page.tsx
findings.description: All timestamps render in UTC with a literal ' UTC' suffix; the target user is in Asia/Riyadh (UTC+3), so a pending budget change whose expiry column shows 14:00 UTC actually expires at 17:00 local - a functional hazard for the approval workflow. Two client components format dates differently and render once on the server (UTC) and again in the browser (local), a React hydration text mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Format in the org/user timezone (default Asia/Riyadh for ar) through a single formatter path with timeZoneName:'short', route the inline toLocaleString calls through formatDate, and compute formatted strings client-side only after mount (or pass pre-formatted strings from the server).

findings.title: 'Remove member' is broken from the dashboard: client sends JSON body, server DELETE reads URL search params
findings.description: The Team page's Remove member action sends a JSON body with no query string, while the server DELETE handler reads organization_id/user_id from the URL search params and zod-parses them as uuids; a null search param fails the uuid parse and throws, so Remove member fails from the dashboard. Confirmed still present at HEAD.
findings.recommendation: Make the client send the ids as query parameters (or make the server read the JSON body); add a regression test exercising the DELETE path.

findings.title: Offboarding/deletion is synchronous, revokes only Google at the IdP, ignores the designed deletion lifecycle, no DSAR export
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/api/deletion/route.ts:13-24 (owner-only; revokes only loadGoogleCredential/revokeGoogleToken then immediate delete from public.organizations)
platform/supabase/migrations/20260817171039_cloud_initial_schema.sql:184+ (deletion_requests table + deletion_status enum designed for async lifecycle, unused)
findings.description: Org deletion hard-deletes immediately, leaving Meta/TikTok/Microsoft/Reddit/etc. OAuth grants live at the provider (only DB rows cascade), and does not use the tracked deletion_requests workflow. There is no GDPR/DSAR data export before deletion.
findings.recommendation: Revoke all provider grants on deletion, drive deletion through the tracked deletion_requests lifecycle, and offer a pre-deletion data export.

findings.title: Enterprise CTA is a mailto to the upstream vendor's personal address in EUR under the 'Adport' brand; upstream brand/persona leak
evidence: 'Adport'/'adport.dev'/'Yannick' embedded in ~40 Arabic strings (accounts.ts, team.ts, support.ts, nav.ts, components/ui.tsx)
findings.description: The only Enterprise upgrade path routes the lead to the upstream vendor's personal mailbox, in euros, under the 'Adport' brand - the product leaves itself at its highest-intent moment. The Arabic UX also carries another product's name and founder throughout the catalogue. Lead routing to a third party is the P3 driver; branding is cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Replace the mailto with an in-product enterprise request (store in feedback, notify via the existing Resend path), rebrand strings behind a {product} placeholder, and add SAR pricing.

findings.title: Arabic terminology inconsistent (provider/org/plan have competing terms); grammar/register calques; needs one glossary + native review
evidence: grep over lib/i18n/messages/*.ts: provider المزوّد 31 vs المنصة 2; org المنظمة 10 vs المؤسسة 4; plan الخطة 8 vs الباقة 2
same key currentPlan resolves to two different Arabic strings across policies.ts vs billing.ts/misc.ts
findings nav الملاحظات vs page title نتائج التدقيق; reports.ts:55 plural '{rows} صفًا' only correct for 11-99
findings.description: The catalogue was written module by module without a glossary, so the same concept has competing Arabic terms and the same English key resolves to different Arabic strings across modules; several entries are grammar/register calques. The parity test checks keys, not vocabulary. Corrections are listed (not applied) in deliverable 07 section 4 and need a native Saudi media-buyer reviewer.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one glossary (provided), apply the grammar/register corrections after native review, and add a vitest that fails on the rejected variants.

findings.title: Arabic typography and RTL defects: non-Arabic monospace labels, negative tracking, physical-CSS billing overlap, bidi reordering
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/globals.css (--font-mono applied with uppercase + positive letter-spacing to every table header/metric label/kicker; 25 negative letter-spacing heading declarations; .plan-features li physical left padding vs ::before inline-start; select background-position:right)
G3 Playwright screenshots show billing checkmark overlap and reordered report summary (VERIFIED_RUNTIME via G3)
findings.description: Arabic labels fall through a monospace stack with no Arabic glyphs, uppercase and positive tracking; 25 negative letter-spacing heading rules pull Arabic joins/marks together; physical-direction CSS leftovers cause a visible billing checkmark overlap and a wrong-side select chevron in RTL (contradicting PHASE2's 'all 32 converted' claim); unicode-bidi:plaintext reorders mixed Arabic/Latin lines and truncates org names from the wrong side.
findings.recommendation: Add an html[lang='ar'] typography layer (Plex Sans Arabic for labels, letter-spacing:0, no uppercase, mono scoped to dir='ltr'/numeric spans), finish the logical-property migration with a stylelint rule, and replace blanket plaintext with <bdi>/dir='ltr' on Latin tokens.

findings.title: Onboarding written for a developer audience, not a buyer; add/enable split, opaque provider dead-end, English titles, no SAR/VAT
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/app/onboarding/onboarding-flow.tsx (mandatory final step adds an MCP server to ChatGPT/Codex/Claude/Cursor/VS Code; built-in Assistant never introduced)
platform/apps/cloud/app/account-selection/page.tsx (picker outside the stepper, no progress bar) vs account-access-manager.tsx (separate enable step)

platform/apps/cloud/lib/i18n/messages/connections.ts:20,57 (single opaque 'Unavailable'/'غير متاح'); app/onboarding/page.tsx:13 (metadata title 'Set up Adport', English); plans.ts (EUR only, no SAR/VAT)
findings.description: A small advertiser must click through 'Add Adport to your agent' before reaching the dashboard, and the product's own Assistant is never introduced. Connecting bounces to /account-selection (outside the stepper) to pick accounts, then back to separately enable each for agent access against the Free cap of 3. Provider cards show one opaque 'Unavailable' that conflates not-configured/rollout-gated/suppressed with no Connect button and no reason; tab titles are English; prices are EUR with no SAR/VAT.
findings.recommendation: Replace/soften the agent step with 'Try the Assistant', embed the account picker in the stepper and merge add/enable, give provider cards distinct states (not-configured/pending-review/rollout-gated/ready), localize metadata via generateMetadata, and add SAR pricing + VAT.

findings.title: IA defaults to a passive read dashboard; the agentic Ask-AI loop is a buried peer tab; no decision/outcome tracking
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/components/nav.tsx (Overview first/landing; Assistant a peer link; no command bar in shell.tsx)
platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/page.tsx (landing is a passive KPI row + campaign table)
platform/apps/cloud/app/dashboard/audit/page.tsx (event-centric; no proposal->applied->outcome chain; engine 'outcome' is RunOutcome plumbing)
findings.description: The product is positioned as an AI media buyer, yet the default surface is a read-only reporting dashboard and the Assistant - the only surface that turns intent into action - is one of eight sidebar links with no shell presence. Nothing closes the loop by showing what an applied change did (before/after spend/CPA/ROAS), so users cannot build trust in the agent's changes. Deliverable 07 section 5 proposes an 'AI Media Buyer Workbench' IA (Ask AI as spine, Morning Brief, Account Health, Opportunities, Approvals, Decisions & Outcomes) mapped to existing engine capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Make Ask AI a persistent composer/command bar in the shell, add a Morning Brief home and an Account Health rollup, surface engine recommendations as an actionable queue into the existing Approvals bridge, and add a Decision History + Outcome Tracking view keyed on applied operations via compare_periods.

key_findings: The 'AI media buyer' is a demo: the engine is pinned to bundled fixture accounts in both demo and live modes (serve_demo.py:386,163), yet the UI calls it 'your connected accounts' - every persona's headline value is undeliverable today (G7-C01).

Three paid/advertised in-product claims are contradicted by code: 'Separate client workspaces' (Agency EUR149/mo live Stripe, unimplemented - G7-C04), 'Includes SSO' (no SAML/OIDC/SCIM - G7-C15), and 'Analyses your connected accounts' (fixtures - G7-C01).

Of 5 personas, only the small single-currency advertiser gets partial value and only as read-only; agency, enterprise and 50-account buyer are structurally BLOCKED (no hierarchy, no org switcher, one grant/provider, flat RBAC, cross-tenant report list, no bulk ops).

The first screen is self-contradictory: the blended ROAS tile is structurally 0x (conversion_value never requested) and spend is summed across currencies while the engine's correct per-currency summary is discarded (G7-C08).

The approver - the one human the safety architecture depends on - sees the least information: a summary string on a 15-minute TTL, no before/after/risk/plans, Apply shown to the requester, no reject reason, no notification (G7-C07).

'Findings' holds a primary nav slot but has no producer anywhere in the codebase, so it is permanently empty (G7-C09); 'Remove member' is broken from the dashboard due to a DELETE body/query mismatch (G7-C19).

Enterprise fails standard procurement: no SSO/SCIM, MFA disabled in config, audit trail capped/unexportable/hard-deleted with nulled actor and no IP, and the only upgrade CTA is a mailto to the upstream vendor's personal address (G7-C15, G7-C16, G7-C21).
All specialist evidence (G1-G6, I2) held under spot-check at HEAD 41b069e; no finding overturned. Only reconciliation: clientWorkspaces severity unified to P1.
G7.disagreements: Specialist-vs-specialist: G6 rated 'Separate client workspaces' P1 while G1 and I2 rated it P2 - reconciled to P1 (G7-C04) because it is a paid feature on live Stripe checkout with zero implementation (serious financial/representation risk per the P1 definition). Code-vs-docs (all VERIFIED_CODE, carried into deliverable 07 section 6): README/assistant.ts 'Analyses connected accounts' is false (engine sample-pin); billing 'Separate client workspaces' and 'Includes SSO' are unimplemented; the overview ROAS footer 'Conversion value / spend' always yields 0; support copy sells retention as 'longer audit history' while the retention cron hard-deletes audit events; PHASE2-REPORT 'all 32 physical direction declarations converted to logical' is false (5 physical shorthands + a background-position:right remain, with a visible billing overlap); ARCHITECTURE/PHASE0 'Approvals page is display-only / no report endpoint' are stale (apply/reject and /reports/run exist); snapchat-live-checklist/PHASE0 reference provider-card '...approval' copy that does not exist (only 'Unavailable'); README 'Arabic by default' omits that Accept-Language wins on first visit; docs/TODO section 7 members DELETE body/query mismatch confirmed still broken.
G7.not_verified: No runtime rendering was performed by G7 (no browser/DB/engine started at HEAD), so all UI/layout/RTL claims are VERIFIED_CODE/VERIFIED_TEST plus G3's earlier Playwright screenshots; current-HEAD rendering is NOT_VERIFIED. Live-LLM Arabic behaviour (MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=live) is NOT_VERIFIED (no model key) - only the fixture-data pin is code-verified. The cross-tenant report leak (G7-C02) is VERIFIED_CODE for the unscoped listReports() call but the leak itself is INFERRED/deployment-dependent (today fixtures; P0 only against a shared-engine real-data production). The *.database.test.ts / database.integration.test.ts suites were not run (no Postgres). Arabic copy quality for a native Saudi media buyer is NOT_VERIFIED - the glossary and grammar corrections are proposals needing a native reviewer. Specialist line numbers predate HEAD 41b069e (reports at f80877c/11784fd) and are substance-accurate, not exact.
