findings.title: No automated backup or restore for any data store (cloud DB, engine DB, workspace)
evidence: docker-compose.yml:78-80 (plain named volumes, no backup sidecar)
findings.description: No pg_dump/WAL/PITR/snapshot/object-store export exists anywhere for the Supabase DB, the engine Postgres (engine-pgdata), or the engine workspace (reports/logs). The only scheduled DB jobs delete data.
findings.recommendation: Use hosted Supabase daily backups + PITR for the cloud DB (retention > data_retention_days); add scheduled logical dumps or managed Postgres+PITR for pma_* and langgraph checkpoints; back up or document-as-reproducible workspace/out. Define RPO/RTO and run a restore drill.
findings.failure_scenario: A lost or corrupted DB volume loses all tenant configuration, encrypted provider credentials, approvals/receipts, and audit history with no recovery path; RPO/RTO are unbounded.
findings.short_summary: No backups/restore for any data store

findings.title: Master encryption key has no KMS/escrow and no working rotation; a restore is useless or a leak
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/crypto.ts:5-9 (single ADPORT_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY, base64->32 bytes; H7 confirmed)
findings.description: Credential confidentiality rests on one symmetric key in an env var. A DB restore without the exact key renders every provider_credentials.ciphertext permanently undecryptable; rotating the key in place would fail every GCM auth tag (self-inflicted data loss). key_version column exists but no code reads it to select a key and no re-encrypt tool exists.
findings.recommendation: Move the key to a KMS/secret manager with its own backup; implement envelope rotation keyed by key_version with a bulk re-encrypt job; document that DR restore must recover the matching key version separately from the DB.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator loses or must rotate the key: all tenants' ad-platform credentials become unrecoverable and every org must reconnect; or a backup bundling the key leaks all credentials.
findings.short_summary: Encryption key: no KMS/escrow, rotation destroys ciphertext

findings.title: No usage metering; the core AI/engine cost is unbilled and uncapped per plan
findings.description: Every Assistant turn and report run forwards to the LLM-driven engine (the dominant variable cost). The only guard is a flat 120 requests/minute per org+user. There is no usage_events table, no per-plan AI/report/token quota, no Stripe metered price. Free reader tier is not blocked from Assistant turns or report GETs.
findings.recommendation: Add a private.usage_events ledger (idempotency-keyed, written in-transaction with each billable action); add per-plan monthly AI/report/token quotas enforced with a 402 PlanLimitError; optionally wire Stripe billMeterEvent for overage; meter engine-returned token usage, not just request counts.
findings.failure_scenario: A single paying org runs 120 engine turns/minute indefinitely on any tier, consuming unbounded model cost the operator cannot bill or cap; margins are unprotected and abuse is undetectable.
findings.short_summary: No usage metering; unbounded per-org AI cost

findings.title: Business cannot contract under its own name: legal/support surfaces route to the upstream third party; no DPA
evidence: platform/website/privacy.html (operated by Yannick Westermann Labs, contact yannick@adport.dev)
findings.description: The privacy policy, terms, in-app support widget, and enterprise CTA all name the upstream vendor as the operating legal entity and sole support contact. No DPA, subprocessor register, or SCCs exist. There is no markting-ai legal entity or support channel anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Replace operator identity, contacts, support routing, and legal documents with markting-ai's own entity; produce a DPA, subprocessor register (Supabase, Stripe, model/provider vendors), and SCCs; sign a flow-down agreement with the upstream vendor if infrastructure is shared.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer's procurement/legal review finds the data controller in the published privacy policy is a third party and support escalations go to one external inbox; the deal cannot close and payment cannot be lawfully taken under markting-ai's name.
findings.short_summary: Legal entity/privacy/terms/support are upstream third party; no DPA

findings.title: No production migration path; only the destructive supabase db reset is documented
evidence: Makefile:25-28 (supabase start + supabase db reset --local --yes is the whole apply path)
findings.description: supabase db reset drops and recreates the entire database. No forward-only production migration command (db push), ordering doc, rollback story, or pg_cron/extension promotion step is defined. The repo's only documented workflow is destructive.
findings.recommendation: Add a forward-only production migration runbook (supabase db push or equivalent) with ordering, pg_cron enablement, pre-migration backup, and tested rollback; explicitly warn that db reset is local-only.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator following the repo's documented migration workflow against production runs db reset and wipes all tenant data; or a bad migration ships with no rollback path.
findings.short_summary: Only destructive db reset documented; no prod migration/rollback

findings.title: No TLS edge / reverse proxy; stack is localhost HTTP only
evidence: no nginx/traefik/caddy service in any compose file
findings.description: The stack terminates no TLS and has no reverse proxy. Secure cookies and OAuth redirect flows that assume HTTPS will not function for any non-local deployment. Correct for a local demo, but a hard prerequisite to serve a remote customer.
findings.recommendation: Add or document a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (traefik/caddy/nginx) with HSTS for any shared/production deployment; this is required before OAuth and secure cookies work.
findings.failure_scenario: Deployed beyond localhost, OAuth redirect and secure-cookie session flows fail and all traffic (including credential exchange) is plaintext.
findings.short_summary: No TLS/reverse proxy; localhost HTTP only

findings.title: No CI at the monorepo root; tenant-isolation DB suite and all glue code are ungated
evidence: find -type d -name workflows => only platform/.github, engine/.github
docs/PHASE0-REPORT.md:24,44 (cites orphaned workflows as live CI)
findings.description: GitHub only runs workflows at <repo-root>/.github/workflows. The git root is the monorepo, which has no .github directory. The six upstream workflows sit in vendored subdirs GitHub never reads, so nothing runs on push/PR. The cross-tenant *.database*.test.ts suites and all net-new glue code (markting bridge, engine-demo host, infra scripts) have zero mechanical gate, and docs cite the orphaned workflows as if live.
findings.recommendation: Author a single root .github/workflows/ci.yml (push+pull_request) running cloud build/typecheck/vitest, a Postgres-backed job for the tenant-isolation DB suites, the engine ruff/mypy/pytest suite, make test, repo-wide gitleaks, and image builds on a networked runner; update docs that cite subdir paths.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in lib/markting/repository.ts or a cross-tenant data-leak in the bridge tables reaches main with no automated check, because the only tests that would catch it never run.
findings.short_summary: No root CI; tenant-isolation tests never run

findings.title: No graceful shutdown or connection draining; no safe zero-downtime deploy
findings.description: There is no shutdown path: no FastAPI lifespan, no uvicorn timeout_graceful_shutdown, and the sync and async Postgres pools are never closed. On SIGTERM uvicorn either waits indefinitely on an in-flight run (routes allow 300s) or is SIGKILLed at the orchestrator grace limit, aborting work mid-flight and tearing down DB connections abruptly.
findings.recommendation: Add a FastAPI lifespan that closes PostgresRepositories and the checkpointer pool; set a bounded uvicorn timeout_graceful_shutdown; make the orchestrator grace period >= that bound.
findings.failure_scenario: A rolling deploy during an active assistant turn or report run either stalls the container stop for minutes or SIGKILLs the process, aborting the run and leaking server-side Postgres connections.
findings.short_summary: No graceful shutdown/drain; unsafe deploys

findings.title: Shared engine state (report index, kill switch) is not cluster-safe
findings.description: The report index is a single global JSON file capped at 50 entries total across all tenants, guarded only by an in-process asyncio.Lock, and the emergency kill switch is a per-process local file. Two engine replicas corrupt the index on concurrent read-modify-write and cannot share the kill switch; a busy tenant evicts others' report history and the cloud route forwards the index unfiltered by org.
findings.recommendation: Move the report index into Postgres keyed by organization (and scope the adport route by organizationId); drop the global 50 cap for per-tenant retention; back the kill switch with shared state (DB row) checked on every write; ensure any file fallback lives on persistent cluster-shared storage.
findings.failure_scenario: With a second engine replica, concurrent report writes corrupt/lose the shared file and engaging the kill switch on one replica does not stop writes on the others; one tenant's reports evict another's.
findings.short_summary: Report index + kill switch not cluster-safe

findings.title: Money-spending apply produces no audit event, structured log, or metric; failures leave the row pending
findings.description: The apply route performs the real ad-account mutation through the adport provider registry (independent of the proposal-only engine) but writes only a pending_operations.status='applied' flag. There is no audit_events row (who/what/when/outcome), no structured log, and no success/failure counter. On failure applyPending throws, markPendingOutcome is skipped, and the row silently stays pending.
findings.recommendation: Emit an audit_events row on both success and failure of apply (actor, org, pendingId, tool, accountId, outcome, latency, error class), a structured log with org/user/request ids, and success/failure counters feeding an alert on elevated apply-failure rate.
findings.failure_scenario: After a budget change spends real money, a post-incident 'who approved and applied this, and did it land?' cannot be answered; a failed apply is invisible to operators and the operation looks still-pending.
findings.short_summary: Apply path unaudited/unlogged; failures silent

findings.title: No metrics anywhere (requests, engine runs, LLM token/cost)
findings.description: No request rate/latency/error metric, no engine run count/duration/outcome metric, and no LLM token or cost metric despite the product being an LLM agent. Nothing records per-org model spend. SLOs are unmeasurable.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal metrics layer (OTel/Prometheus): request count/latency/error by route+status, engine run count/duration/outcome, apply success/failure counters, and per-org token/estimated-cost counters.
findings.failure_scenario: A latency regression, error spike, saturation, or runaway model cost in production goes undetected; capacity planning and per-tenant cost attribution are impossible.
findings.short_summary: No metrics (request/engine/token-cost)

findings.title: No alerting on failures, health-down, cost anomalies, or 5xx
findings.description: There is no alerting mechanism anywhere: no page on sustained apply-failure rate, engine /health down, model/cost anomaly, or 5xx spike.
findings.recommendation: Add alerting on apply-failure rate, /health/readiness down, cost anomalies, and 5xx spikes once metrics exist.
findings.failure_scenario: An outage or a surge in failed ad-account writes continues until a customer reports it, because nothing pages the operator.
findings.short_summary: No alerting on failures/health/cost

findings.title: No distributed tracing; LangSmith tracing documented but not enabled, write path untraced
findings.description: Modern LangSmith SDKs require an explicit tracing flag in addition to the API key; the project sets/documents none, so the key alone yields no traces. Even enabled, LangSmith covers only engine LangGraph runs; the cloud->engine apply path (where real writes happen) is never traced.
findings.recommendation: Wire and document the tracing flag explicitly or correct the docs; add first-party trace-id propagation across cloud->engine->provider so an apply can be followed end-to-end.
findings.failure_scenario: Operators following the docs believe runs are traced when they are not, and a failing apply cannot be followed across cloud and engine.
findings.short_summary: Tracing documented not enabled; write path untraced

findings.title: Unstructured logs with no tenant/trace context; inconsistent cloud logging and weaker redaction
findings.description: Engine logs are plaintext with no thread/org/trace id and barely used; cloud log sites are half JSON half free-form, none carry org/user/request ids, and there is no request access log on either runtime. Cloud redaction is narrower than the engine's and http.ts logs raw errors unredacted, so a provider error embedding an AIza../sk-../pb_.. token or a postgres:// DSN can be written verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one structured JSON logger per service with org/user/request/trace/thread ids on every record; add request-level access logs via Next middleware and FastAPI middleware; share a redaction utility mirroring the engine patterns and apply it in http.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: An incident cannot be correlated across a request or traced to a tenant, and a leaked credential in upstream error text is persisted to log aggregation.
findings.short_summary: Unstructured, context-free logs; weak cloud redaction

findings.title: Health endpoint is liveness treated as readiness; cloud service has no healthcheck; /markting/info over-discloses
evidence: docker-compose.yml cloud.depends_on.engine.condition: service_healthy treats it as readiness
H7: compose healthchecks only at :56 engine, :73 engine-db (cloud none)
findings.description: /health returns static runtime metadata and never pings Postgres or the model, so it stays 200 with a dead DB while the orchestrator keeps routing traffic that fails at request time. The cloud service has no healthcheck at all. /markting/info is unauthenticated and leaks approver references and account aliases plus the write-safety posture.
findings.recommendation: Split liveness (/health, cheap) from readiness (/ready, pings Postgres SELECT 1 + pool saturation); point compose/depends_on at readiness; add a cloud healthcheck; require the bearer caller dependency on /markting/info or strip approvers/aliases.
findings.failure_scenario: Postgres is down but containers report healthy; the cloud routes requests that all 500, and an unauthenticated caller enumerates approver identities and account aliases for reconnaissance.
findings.short_summary: Liveness-as-readiness; no cloud healthcheck; /markting/info leaks

findings.title: markting_* bridge tables and the engine DB have no retention (unbounded growth)
findings.description: The newest migration adds four tenant tables (markting_engine_proposals full proposal+translation JSONB, markting_threads one row per conversation, sandbox state, aliases) but never extends apply_data_retention(). The engine Postgres (checkpoints, pma_*, pma_dedupe) has no retention at all. The documented data_retention_days guarantee silently does not apply to them.
findings.recommendation: Add markting_engine_proposals (by created_at), markting_threads (by last_message_at), and sandbox state to apply_data_retention() keyed on data_retention_days with a covering delete index; implement engine-side retention (old checkpoints/dedupe) or document that engine-db has none; add tests asserting per-table pruning.
findings.failure_scenario: Per-tenant conversation provenance and ad-change JSONB grow forever; storage and the engine DB grow unbounded, and tenant data the retention policy is meant to bound is never deleted.
findings.short_summary: markting_* + engine DB excluded from retention

findings.title: Cloud pool max:10 with direct (non-pooler) URL unsafe on serverless; no statement/idle timeouts
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/.env.example:5 (SUPABASE_DB_URL on direct port, not 6543 pooler)
findings.description: On Vercel each warm function instance opens its own pool of up to 10 connections against the direct Postgres port; many instances multiply against the connection limit. The sample env points at the direct URL. No statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is set on any client or role, so a hung query or abandoned transaction pins a connection indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: For serverless require the Supabase transaction pooler URL with a low max (1-3); set statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on adport_backend and the engine user; document per-target pool math.
findings.failure_scenario: Under load a Vercel deployment with the direct URL exhausts Postgres connections (too many clients), and a single hung query holds a pooled connection open with no server-side timeout.
findings.short_summary: Serverless pool math unsafe; no statement/idle timeouts

findings.title: Stripe webhook idempotency not atomic, no ordering guard, no dunning; past_due keeps full access
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/billing.ts:119-138 (dedup select + billing_events insert outside the applySubscription transaction)
findings.description: processStripeEvent checks billing_events, calls applySubscription (its own txn), then inserts the event id afterward, so two concurrent deliveries can both apply and a crash between commit and insert reprocesses. applySubscription always overwrites plan/status from the current event with no ordering/recency guard, so a stale event can regress entitlement. There is no payment_failed/dunning path and past_due retains full engine access.
findings.recommendation: Insert billing_events inside the applySubscription transaction with on conflict do nothing (0 rows = duplicate skip); add an ordering/recency guard (store Stripe created/last_event_at or re-fetch authoritative state); define an explicit dunning policy driven by invoice.payment_failed.
findings.failure_scenario: A Stripe retry double-processes an event (duplicate audit/downscale) or a late out-of-order event re-activates a canceled plan; a delinquent customer keeps full paid (and unmetered-cost) access through the dunning window.
findings.short_summary: Webhook non-atomic/unordered; no dunning

findings.title: No server-side request timeout and a process-wide report lock cause cross-tenant head-of-line blocking
evidence: services/engine-demo/serve_demo.py:324,344-353 (report runs inside a single async with lock)
findings.description: The engine has no per-request server-side timeout; a client abort cancels only the fetch, not the server coroutine, so aborted requests leave orphaned engine work. Reports run inside a single process-wide asyncio.Lock, so one slow report (e.g. WeasyPrint render) blocks all other report runs in that process.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the engine handler in asyncio.wait_for with a server budget below the client timeout; make the report lock finer-grained or replace with DB-level concurrency; honor client disconnects.
findings.failure_scenario: One stuck WeasyPrint PDF render stalls the report surface for all tenants, and client-aborted requests continue burning engine compute.
findings.short_summary: No server timeout; process-wide report lock blocks all tenants

findings.title: No image build or repo-wide secret scan in any pipeline; gitleaks engine-only and orphaned
evidence: engine/.github/workflows/ci.yml:37-56 (gitleaks scans engine subtree only, orphaned)
three Dockerfiles built by no workflow
docs/TODO.md:21 (CI docker builds + secret scanning listed as open)
findings.description: No workflow builds the cloud/engine/sandbox images, so none is proven buildable per-commit. The only gitleaks job runs from engine/ and scans only the engine subtree history; nothing scans the platform/, infra/, services/, or docs/ history where the glue, infra scripts, and .env.example live. Dependabot configs sit at subdir paths GitHub won't read from root.
findings.recommendation: Add a root gitleaks job scanning the whole monorepo history (fetch-depth 0, SHA-pinned binary) and a docker-build job for cloud+engine on a networked runner; relocate dependabot configs to root; pin action versions consistently.
findings.failure_scenario: A credential committed anywhere outside engine/ is never caught, and a Dockerfile break ships because no commit ever builds the images.
findings.short_summary: No image build / repo-wide secret scan in CI

findings.title: Cloud build context has no .dockerignore; a gitignored .env.local and 577MB node_modules enter the build
findings.description: The cloud image copies the entire ./platform tree with no ignore list, baking a developer's gitignored apps/cloud/.env.local into a build-stage layer and shipping 577MB of host node_modules/.turbo into the builder. Multi-stage output limits but does not eliminate the leak (intermediate layer retains secrets if pushed/cached; standalone tracing can pick up .env*).
findings.recommendation: Add platform/.dockerignore excluding node_modules, .next, .turbo, .git, **/.env, **/.env.* (keep .env.example), website, docs, supabase; confirm .env.local is never traced into .next/standalone.
findings.failure_scenario: If a build-stage image is pushed or cached, a developer's real secret keys and 577MB of host artifacts are embedded in the layer.
findings.short_summary: No .dockerignore; secrets + node_modules in build context

findings.title: Engine container runs as root; no resource limits, grace periods, or healthcheck start_period
evidence: H7: grep -n USER engine/Dockerfile => none (only infra/cloud.Dockerfile:22 USER node)
findings.description: The engine image sets no USER so it runs as UID 0 (the cloud image correctly drops to node). No service in either compose file sets CPU/memory limits, stop_grace_period, or healthcheck start_period, and restart: unless-stopped has no backoff cap. A runaway report render can OOM the host.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-root user to engine/Dockerfile (create user, chown workspace, USER); set mem/cpu limits + reservations, stop_grace_period aligned with the graceful-shutdown bound, and healthcheck start_period; cap restart behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A container-escape/RCE in the engine runs as root; a memory-heavy render grows unbounded and OOMs the host, taking down engine and cloud with no blast-radius containment.
findings.short_summary: Engine runs as root; no resource limits/grace/start_period

findings.title: Key rotation and enterprise provisioning are schema/doc-provisioned but not implemented
findings.description: Groundwork exists (key_version column, an enterprise entry in PLANS) but neither is wired: there is no multi-key decrypt/re-encrypt path, and enterprise has no Stripe price, checkout, or admin UI (only a DBA direct write), while advertised SSO/regional hosting/SLA/dedicated onboarding have no implementation. These are only hard blockers when selling enterprise; for a first non-enterprise customer they are quality/maintainability gaps plus a mis-selling risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement envelope rotation keyed by key_version; add an enterprise provisioning path (custom Stripe price mapped in planForPrice or an internal admin console) with audit+lifecycle; implement the sold enterprise features behind the entitlement or remove the claims until shipped.
findings.failure_scenario: An enterprise bought on SSO/residency/SLA promises cannot be delivered and requires manual DB surgery to provision; the key cannot be rotated after compromise.
findings.short_summary: Key rotation + enterprise provisioning claimed, not built

key_findings: System is NOT ready for a first paying customer; the repo's own docs (deployment-model.md:49-58, TODO.md:18-22) enumerate the unmet gates, and the P1 blockers are acknowledged rather than hidden.

The shipped compose stack is a local proposal-only demo (writes disabled, sample data, Supabase excluded, plain HTTP); accepting a paying customer requires a production topology that does not exist in the repo and could not be built/run in this sandbox.

The cloud 'apply' path (approvals/[id]/apply/route.ts:26) writes to real ad accounts through the adport registry independently of the proposal-only engine, yet has no audit row, log, or metric (recordAudit count 0) - the money-spending mutation is the least observable step.

Seven hard P1 blockers: no backups/DR, no KMS/key-escrow (unrecoverable/unrotatable key), no usage metering (unbounded AI cost), legal/support surfaces are an upstream third party with no DPA, destructive-only migration path, no TLS edge, no root CI (tenant-isolation DB suite never runs).

Operability P1s the moment the engine goes live or scales: no graceful shutdown/drain, and shared state (global 50-cap report index file, per-process kill-switch file) that corrupts/desyncs across replicas.
Zero observability: no metrics, no tracing (LangSmith key present but tracing flag never set), no alerting, unstructured context-free logs; SLOs are unmeasurable as shipped.

All eight specialist reports (H1-H6, I3, I4) held under spot-check with correct classifications and no severity inflation; I made only two frame-dependent severity promotions (migration path, TLS edge to P1) and one impact clarification (demo safety does not cover the cloud apply path).
H7.disagreements: No disagreements among the eight specialist reports; they corroborate each other. Disagreements between the code and project docs: (1) PHASE0-REPORT.md:24,44 and ARCHITECTURE.md:863 present .github/workflows/ci.yml as live CI, but no CI runs at the monorepo root (H2). (2) deployment-model.md:38 implies tenant-data retention is enforced, but markting_* bridge tables and the engine DB are not covered by apply_data_retention() (H5-01/S7). (3) deployment-model.md:45 implies ciphertext records a usable key version for rotation, but repository.ts:162 hardcodes key_version=1 and no code reads it (B2/H6-03). (4) i18n/messages/billing.ts:58 sells SSO/regional-hosting/SLA/dedicated-onboarding; only custom retention is implemented (I4-02). (5) privacy.html/terms.html name Yannick Westermann Labs / adport.dev as operator and sole contact, so markting-ai cannot contract under its own name (B4/I4-03). Where docs are honest: TODO.md:18-22 and deployment-model.md:49-58 correctly list backups, KMS, monitoring/alerting, CI, legal docs, OAuth verification, and tested runbooks as unmet gates.
H7.not_verified: Docker image builds and docker compose up runtime (sandbox network-blocked, not retried): whether any Dockerfile builds, whether next build traces .env.local into .next/standalone (H7-P3-1 leak reach is INFERRED), real SIGTERM graceful-shutdown behaviour, event-loop blocking under load, and WeasyPrint OOM footprint are all INFERRED from code, not measured. Live Stripe: no webhook exercised end-to-end (no keys/signatures); database.integration.test.ts not run (needs live Supabase DB), so the downscaling/canceled transition is VERIFIED_CODE+test-exists, not VERIFIED_RUNTIME; the concurrent-webhook double-processing race (S9) is a code-path inference. Live OAuth (Google/Meta/TikTok/etc.): no provider approval, redirect URIs, or token exchange tested; the Apple ES256 delegated flow is NOT_VERIFIED. Managed-Supabase platform backups/PITR and whether the two pg_cron jobs actually run in production are out-of-repo settings, NOT_VERIFIED. Committed config.toml disables MFA/TOTP and pins region us; whether the production project overrides these is DOCUMENTED_ONLY. The Node/pnpm cloud suites (vitest/typecheck/build) were unexecutable here because corepack cannot fetch pnpm offline (H2-08), so their green status is NOT_VERIFIED by me; the uv/Python half is runnable but I ran only targeted read-only checks as this workstream is consolidation, not test execution.

I5.scope: Led the I-series (SaaS monetization, agency workflow, billing/usage-metering, enterprise packaging). Read I1-I4 in full, independently spot-checked each specialist's load-bearing claims against code, and produced /home/user/markting-ai/docs/audit/_business-and-pricing-architecture.md plus /home/user/markting-ai/docs/audit/agents/I5.md. Findings below are the consolidated, deduplicated team findings with final severities.

sed -n billing.ts => exit 0 (planForPrice omits enterprise; non-atomic webhook dedup)

rg listReports|runReport|fetchReportFile engine-client.ts => exit 0 (no org scope)
grep currency|automatic_tax|tax stripe-setup.mjs => exit 0 (CURRENCY=eur, tax-exclusive)
rg automatic_tax|vat|sar|zatca platform/apps/cloud => exit 0 (no hits)
grep enterpriseIncludes|SSO|featureClientWorkspaces i18n/billing.ts => exit 0 (claims confirmed)
grep VAT|automatic_tax|sar docs/billing.md => exit 0 (VAT/SAR documented as deferred decisions)

findings.title: No AI/engine usage metering; the product's dominant variable cost is uncapped on every plan
evidence: rg -niE usage_event|meter|quota|billMeterEvent over platform/apps/cloud => exit 0, no hits
findings.description: The product is an AI media buyer; every Assistant turn and report run invokes the LLM engine, yet the only guard is a flat plan-independent 120 req/min rate limit. Free reader and past_due orgs reach the engine. No usage_events ledger, no per-plan AI/report/token quota, no Stripe metered billing exists anywhere in the cloud app. Merges I1-01, I1-02, I3-01.
findings.recommendation: Add a private.usage_events append-only ledger written in-transaction with each billable action, per-plan quota columns enforced with 402 PlanLimitError, and optional Stripe billMeterEvent overage; capture token/cost from the engine response.

findings.title: Enterprise tier is unsellable: no provisioning path and advertised features unimplemented
findings.description: planForPrice maps only operator/premium/agency; any enterprise price is rejected, so enterprise can only be granted by a manual DB write. Four of five advertised differentiators (SSO, regional hosting, SLA, dedicated onboarding) have no implementation; only custom retention is real. Merges I4-01, I4-02.
findings.recommendation: Add an enterprise provisioning path (custom Stripe price/invoice + internal admin console with lifecycle+audit) and implement or remove each advertised capability.

findings.title: Pervasive upstream (Adport/Yannick) branding and legal operator identity on revenue and legal surfaces
findings.description: The enterprise sales CTA (mailto:yannick@adport.dev), the in-app support widget (Yannick from Adport / Talk to Yannick), and the published privacy/terms name Yannick Westermann Labs as the operating legal entity and sole contact. No markting-ai legal entity, support channel, or Arabic-market contact exists. Merges I1-05, I4-03.
findings.recommendation: Replace operator identity, contacts, support routing and legal docs with markting-ai's own entity; make the enterprise contact env-configurable; produce a DPA and subprocessor register.

findings.title: Single shared engine instance; report list/fetch unscoped by org, potential cross-tenant exposure
findings.description: The engine client is one deployment-wide MARKTING_ENGINE_URL+TOKEN with no org parameter; runReport/listReports/fetchReportFile carry no org/account scope and the reports route calls listReports() directly. Per-client reporting is impossible, and a shared-engine multi-tenant deployment would let any org read others' report runs. From I2-04.
findings.failure_scenario: A real engine pointed at a multi-tenant cloud deployment: org B calls GET /api/reports/engine and receives org A's report runs and can stream their files via fetchReportFile, since only membership of an org (not report ownership) is checked. Would be P0 if confirmed in production.
findings.recommendation: Scope every engine call per org/client (tenant id or per-tenant token) and filter listReports/fetchReportFile by the caller's org; add a test asserting an org cannot read another org's report run.

findings.title: clientWorkspaces is advertised and billed (Agency) with zero implementation
findings.description: The clientWorkspaces flag (true for agency/enterprise) is rendered only as the billing bullet 'Separate client workspaces'; no code branches on it. A paying Agency customer (EUR 149/mo) is charged for a capability the code does not provide. Merges I1-03, I2-01.
findings.recommendation: Implement client-scoped sub-workspaces and gate on the flag, or remove the flag, bullet, and plan copy until shipped.

findings.title: No agency/client hierarchy, per-client access scoping, white-label, or org switcher
findings.description: The data model is a flat single-tenant org: one org+owner per signup, no client/group column, org-wide RLS visibility, no org switcher UI (users pinned to oldest membership), no white-label/branding, and approvals are an internal maker-checker gate not external client sign-off. Merges I2-02/03/05/06/07.
findings.recommendation: Add a first-class clients entity with per-account role assignments enforced in RLS and the bridge runtime; org-level branding; an org switcher with persisted active org.

findings.title: Churned customers are locked out of in-app re-subscription
findings.description: startSubscription throws whenever entitlement.providerSubscriptionId is set; on customer.subscription.deleted the dead subscription id is written and never cleared, and getOrganizationEntitlement returns it regardless of status. The portal cannot resurrect a deleted subscription, so a churned org has no self-serve path back to paid. From I3-02.
findings.failure_scenario: Org fully cancels -> row keeps provider_subscription_id with status canceled -> owner clicks Start trial -> actions.ts:19 throws 'Manage the existing subscription in the billing portal' -> portal has no deleted subscription to manage -> stuck on Free.
findings.recommendation: Gate startSubscription on an active-ish status (active/trialing/past_due/unpaid) rather than mere presence of providerSubscriptionId, or clear provider_subscription_id on customer.subscription.deleted while keeping provider_customer_id.

findings.title: Webhook dedup is not atomic with its effect and has no ordering/recency guard
findings.description: processStripeEvent does a dedup select, then applySubscription (its own transaction), then a separate billing_events insert afterward; the read and effect are not in one transaction. applySubscription also unconditionally overwrites plan/status from whatever event arrives with no recency comparison. Merges I3-03, I3-04.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent Stripe retries of the same event both pass the dedup select and both run applySubscription (duplicate audit events / re-downscale); or a stale customer.subscription.updated delivered after a newer one overwrites the row with older plan/status, regressing entitlement.
findings.recommendation: Insert the billing_events row inside the effect transaction (on conflict do nothing; treat 0 rows as duplicate), and guard updates with the subscription's Stripe created/last_event_at or re-fetch authoritative state.

findings.title: past_due retains full entitlement; no dunning or payment-failure downgrade
findings.description: past_due is treated as fully entitled, and there is no invoice.payment_failed handler; the code relies solely on Stripe eventually sending unpaid/canceled. Combined with I5-01 a delinquent org keeps uncapped paid (AI-cost) access for the whole dunning window. Merges I1-06, I3-05.
findings.recommendation: Define a grace window and soft-lock write/automation on past_due with an in-app payment-failed banner, independent of Stripe retry config.

findings.title: No audit export; audit UI capped at 150 rows despite selling 3650-day retention
findings.description: Events are retained up to 10 years and purged daily, but only the last 150 are viewable with no pagination, filter, search, CSV/JSON export, or API endpoint. The sold custom-retention value is unrealizable. From I4-04.
findings.recommendation: Add a paginated/filterable audit view and an authenticated streamed CSV/JSON export endpoint, admin-gated.

findings.title: No data residency; privacy policy affirms international processing versus the regional-hosting claim
findings.description: The product runs against a single fixed-region Supabase project; there is no per-tenant region selection, and the published privacy policy affirmatively allows cross-border processing, contradicting the sold 'regional hosting'. From I4-05.
findings.recommendation: Offer region-pinned deployments (separate Supabase projects per region) and a DPA residency commitment; stop advertising regional hosting until available.

findings.title: No SSO (SAML/OIDC) or SCIM; MFA disabled in committed config
findings.description: Authentication is password + Google/GitHub social only; no SAML/OIDC, no SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning, and TOTP/phone MFA enroll is disabled in the committed config. Standard enterprise identity/offboarding gates are unmet. Merges I4-06, I4-07.
findings.recommendation: Add SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM gated to the enterprise entitlement; enforce MFA for admin/owner roles with step-up on apply/delete; confirm the production project matches.

findings.title: No DPA or subprocessor register; legal docs upstream-branded and flagged as unmet production gates
findings.description: Enterprise contracting needs a DPA, subprocessor list, and SCCs; none exist, and the repo's own deployment doc lists privacy/terms/deletion/subprocessor records as still-required production gates. From I4-08.
findings.recommendation: Produce a markting-ai DPA, subprocessor register (Supabase, Stripe, model/provider vendors), and SCCs.

findings.title: Entitlement is a thin inline DTO; no overrides/flags/trials/credits; enterprise limits hard-coded null
findings.description: getOrganizationEntitlement is a single-row read mapped to the hard-coded PLANS object; the principal carries only planId/planName/writeAccess; every call site indexes PLANS directly. No per-org override, feature-flag, trial/credit/grandfather mechanism; enterprise limits are null in code, not negotiated data. From I1-04.
findings.recommendation: Extract a central resolveEntitlement(org) that merges plan defaults with entitlement_overrides and feature_flags; make limits data, not code.

findings.title: Downgrade reconciles only active accounts; members and retention are not reclaimed
findings.description: On downgrade the webhook clamps active ad accounts only; members and retention are enforced at mutation time, so a downgraded org keeps all existing seats and its previous retention window indefinitely. From I1-07.
findings.recommendation: On downgrade, reconcile members/retention to the new ceiling with notice, or explicitly document grandfathering as intended policy.

findings.title: Demo seed grants a paid plan by direct DB write with no environment guard
findings.description: The demo seed bypasses Stripe and sets plan=operator, status=active directly, with no NODE_ENV/host guard preventing it being pointed at a production DB. The seeded org has no provider_subscription_id so billing never reconciles it. From I3-06.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs node infra/seed/seed-demo.mjs with a prod .env -> an org is granted a free, Stripe-less paid plan that webhooks never reconcile.
findings.recommendation: Guard the seed (refuse unless the DB URL is localhost or an explicit allow flag is set) and document that seeded orgs are unbilled.

findings.title: applySubscription trusts subscription.metadata.organizationId without binding it to the customer
findings.description: When metadata.organizationId is present it is used directly as the target org, skipping the customer/subscription lookup, with no check that the customer belongs to that org. Low risk (metadata is first-party, events are signature-verified) but removes defense-in-depth and can throw a unique-violation on mismatch. From I3-07.
findings.recommendation: After resolving via metadata, assert the resolved org's stored provider_customer_id is null or equals the event's customer id before overwriting.

findings.title: Trial abuse: unlimited orgs yield unlimited 7-day trials
findings.description: The 7-day trial is one per org, but trials are tracked per org and a user can obtain multiple orgs, each with its own trial. From I3.
findings.failure_scenario: A user repeatedly creates organizations and starts a fresh 7-day trial in each, consuming paid-cost engine capacity without ever paying.
findings.recommendation: Add trial-abuse controls keyed on customer or payment method rather than per org.

findings.title: VAT (KSA 15%) uncollected, EUR tax-exclusive, SAR not offered - explicit deferred open decisions
findings.description: Pricing is EUR, tax-exclusive, with no automatic_tax and no VAT/SAR/ZATCA code anywhere. docs/billing.md documents KSA 15% VAT and a SAR switch as decisions explicitly left to the operator. For an Arabic-first product this is part of a wider Gulf-readiness cluster (residency, Arabic legal docs).
findings.recommendation: Decide Stripe Tax + automatic_tax (VAT/OSS) and SAR/multi-currency pricing; ZATCA e-invoicing is a separate larger decision. Do not change pricing without operator direction.

findings.title: Webhook entitlement transitions lack fast unit coverage
findings.description: The most financially sensitive code (subscriptionStatus mapping, account downscaling boundaries, getOrganizationEntitlement thresholds) is covered only by a DB-backed integration test; there is no fast unit coverage, so regressions can ship where the integration DB is absent. From I3-08.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for subscriptionStatus over all Stripe statuses, downgrade boundaries, and the slice(maxActiveAccounts) downscaling math with off-by-one cases.

findings.title: API/MCP access is not an enterprise differentiator and has no per-plan key cap
findings.description: createApiKey has no plan gate or key-count cap, and hosted MCP+REST is available on all tiers. There is no enterprise-specific API tier, quota, or per-org key ceiling. From I4-10.
findings.recommendation: Define enterprise API entitlements (quotas, dedicated throughput) and per-plan key limits if API access is used as a selling point.

key_findings: No usage metering for AI/engine inference, the product's dominant variable cost: every Assistant turn and report runs an LLM guarded only by a flat 120 req/min rate limit, and Free/past_due orgs reach the engine uncapped (P1 financial risk).

The Enterprise tier is unsellable: planForPrice omits enterprise so it can only be granted by a manual DB write, and advertised SSO/regional hosting/SLA/dedicated onboarding are unimplemented (only custom retention is real).

Revenue and legal surfaces still carry the upstream vendor's identity: the enterprise CTA emails yannick@adport.dev, the support widget is 'Yannick from Adport', and privacy/terms name Yannick Westermann Labs as the operating legal entity, so markting-ai cannot contract under its own name.

clientWorkspaces is advertised and billed on the Agency tier (EUR 149/mo) but has zero functional implementation; the entire data model is a flat single-tenant org with no client hierarchy, per-client scoping, white-label, or org switcher.

The engine is one deployment-wide URL+token and report list/fetch carry no org scope, making per-client reporting impossible and risking cross-tenant report exposure on any shared-engine deployment (P1, P0 if confirmed in prod).

Entitlement is a thin inline DTO over a hard-coded PLANS object with no overrides, feature flags, trials, or credits, so any pricing change requires a code change and redeploy; enterprise limits are null-in-code, not negotiated data.

VAT (KSA 15%) and SAR are explicit, documented, deferred open decisions: pricing is EUR tax-exclusive with no automatic_tax and no ZATCA code, a Gulf-readiness gap alongside data residency and Arabic legal docs.

Billing plumbing is real but has reliability/revenue gaps: non-atomic webhook dedup with no ordering guard, churned customers locked out of in-app re-subscription, past_due keeps full entitlement with no dunning, and no audit export despite a 10-year retention sale.
I5.disagreements: i18n/billing.ts:58 sells 'SSO, regional hosting, SLA, dedicated onboarding' but only custom retention is implemented (VERIFIED_CODE). The billing UI and plan copy sell 'Separate client workspaces' with no implementation (VERIFIED_CODE). platform/website/privacy.html:21 and terms.html:21 present a live managed service while naming a third party (Yannick Westermann Labs) as the legal operator and sole contact (VERIFIED_CODE). platform/docs/deployment-model.md:3 presents a deployment model while :55 lists privacy/terms/subprocessor/residency as still-required gates, so the enterprise posture is pre-production (DOCUMENTED_ONLY). docs/billing.md:7,27 imply full plan enforcement, but the listed clientWorkspaces dimension is inert and neither billing.md nor ARCHITECTURE.md acknowledges the absence of AI usage metering - a material omission for an AI media buyer. docs/billing.md:21,41 honestly flag VAT and SAR as unimplemented open decisions, which matches the code (no contradiction).
I5.not_verified: No runtime verification was possible: no live Stripe webhook round-trip, no running Supabase (I3's database.integration.test.ts not executed here), and no live engine. Therefore the cross-tenant report leak (I5-04) remains INFERRED/deployment-dependent and the concurrent-webhook double-processing race (I5-08) is a code-path inference rather than a demonstrated race. Not verified whether the hosted production Supabase project overrides config.toml to enable MFA/SSO or pin a region (committed config says disabled/us). Not verified whether the engine emits per-run token/cost usage that a metering layer could capture (engine host is outside this workstream's file scope). Not verified whether an out-of-repo admin tool exists to set plan=enterprise. Trial-abuse-via-multiple-orgs is inferred from the per-org subscription model, not exercised.
